item.title: Parameter-Free First-Order Method for Constrained Variational Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2611.00229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Constrained variational inequalities (VIs) provide a general framework for modeling and solving complementarity and equilibrium problems with functional constraints. In this paper, we propose a parameter-free accelerated operator sliding (PFAOS) method for solving monotone VIs with convex smooth constraints. For a single constraint, PFAOS achieves an operator evaluation complexity of $\mathcal{O}(1/\varepsilon)$ and a constraint gradient evaluation complexity of $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{\varepsilon})$, without requiring prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant of the VI operator or the smoothness constant of the constraint function. We further extend PFAOS to multiple constraints by incorporating a primal-dual hybrid gradient update, yielding a multi-constrained PFAOS (MC-PFAOS) method that preserves the same evaluation complexities. Finally, numerical experiments are conducted on large-scale games with coupling constraints to validate the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Yan Wu, Qi Luo, Yuyuan Ouyang

item.title: A Preconditioned Semismooth Newton Method for Box-Constrained Elliptic Optimal Control Problems with Random Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.00246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the optimal control problem of an elliptic PDE with random diffusion under pointwise box constraints on the control. The constraints make the optimality conditions nonsmooth, with an active set that is not known in advance, and the random diffusion couples the state and the adjoint across all stochastic modes. To design a solution algorithm for this problem, we rely on the Fenchel duality viewpoint. Fenchel duality absorbs the box constraint into the objective and yields an exact reduced problem in the elliptic adjoint variable alone. After a stochastic Galerkin--finite element discretization, eliminating the state leaves a strongly monotone, piecewise smooth equation, which we solve directly by a matrix-free semismooth Newton method with the box projection retained exactly and with no outer iteration, penalty or smoothing parameter. Next, we introduce and analyze a current-set preconditioner, which adds the active-set correction of the current Newton step to a mean-diffusion reference operator and is inverted exactly by a rank-1 update. For implementation, we use a cheaper preconditioner that keeps only a fraction of free control values. Numerical experiments show second-order convergence of the state, and Newton and PCG counts that stay bounded under mesh refinement and growth of the stochastic dimension.
item.dc:creator: Zhendong Li, Akwum Onwunta, Hailing Wang

item.title: Costate Estimation and Covector Mapping for Bernstein Polynomial Direct Methods in Optimal Control
item.description: arXiv:2611.00250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bernstein polynomial approximation of continuous functions has a slower rate of convergence as compared to other approximation methods. ``The fact seems to have precluded any numerical application of Bernstein polynomials from having been made. Perhaps they will find application when the properties of the approximant in the large are of more importance than the closeness of the approximation.'' -- has remarked P.J. Davis in his 1963 book Interpolation and Approximation. This paper presents a direct approximation method for nonlinear optimal control problems with mixed input and state constraints based on Bernstein polynomial approximation, in which the dynamic and path constraints are imposed at the Bernstein coefficients (control points). We provide a rigorous analysis showing that, under convergence assumptions on the control polygons, the proposed method yields consistent approximations of time continuous optimal control problems and can be used for costate estimation of the optimal control problems. In particular, multipliers satisfying a relaxed Karush Kuhn Tucker system of the resulting nonlinear program, scaled by the quadrature weight, approximate the costate and the multipliers of the optimal control problem. Owing to the structure of the Bernstein differentiation matrix, the discrete transversality conditions are contained in the relaxed Karush Kuhn Tucker system, and no additional closure conditions need to be added to it. This result leads to the formulation of the Covector Mapping Theorem for Bernstein polynomial approximation.
item.dc:creator: Venanzio Cichella, Isaac Kaminer, Claire Walton, Naira Hovakimyan, Antonio Pascoal

item.title: Porteous Meets Walsh: Counting Critical Points for $\mathcal{H}_2$-Norm Model Order Reduction Using Algebraic Geometry Behind Multiparameter Eigenvalue Problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.00258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Several polynomial systems arising in systems and control have been shown to exhibit a partially linear structure, which allows them to be reformulated as a multiparameter eigenvalue problem (MEP). In this work, we show how such MEP formulations can be leveraged to obtain refined information about the solution set of the polynomial system. We demonstrate, in the setting of single-input single-output $\mathcal{H}_2$-norm model order reduction, how the Thom--Porteous formula can be used to derive an exact count of the complex solutions of the critical equations derived from Walsh's theorem. We prove, under suitable genericity assumptions, that their set of complex solutions is finite and that all solutions occur without multiplicity. Moreover, we derive an explicit formula for the total number of complex solutions as a function of the model orders. Throughout, we provide a self-contained and application-oriented exposition of the algebro-geometric tools required for our analysis, with the aim of making them accessible to the broader engineering community.
item.dc:creator: Sibren Lagauw, Leonie Kayser, Bart De Moor

item.title: Variance-reduced First-order Methods for Finite-sum Function Constrained Convex Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.00317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies finite-sum convex optimization with convex function constraints, where both the objective $f(x)=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)$ and the constraint mapping $g(x)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n g_j(x)$ may have a large number of components. We propose a variance-reduced anchored constraint extrapolation method (VaRAn-ConEx), which combines stochastic component sampling with primal--dual extrapolation for nonlinear function constraints. Relative to stochastic approximation schemes such as ConEx, VaRAn-ConEx~method reduces gradient complexity by using epoch-wise full-gradient correction and variance-reduced estimators for both the objective and constraint components. In the semi-finite case where $n=1$, the method attains gradient complexities $O(\sqrt m/\epsilon)$ under constant steps and $O(m/\epsilon^{1/2}+1/\epsilon^{3/2})$ under nonconstant steps. In the fully finite-sum case, we establish boundedness of the Lagrange multiplier sequence and derive convergence and gradient-complexity bounds for constant and nonconstant step-size policies. Under these policies, we then prove similar gradient complexity with $m$ replaced by $\max\{m,n\}$. We also show acceleration when the finite-sum objective $f$ is strongly convex, irrespective of components $f_i$.
item.dc:creator: Yasin Gharehmohammadlou, Digvijay Boob

item.title: Optimistic Gradient Algorithms with Randomized Coordinate and Variance Reduction Strategies for Composite Inclusions
item.description: arXiv:2611.00334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider a class of possibly nonmonotone finite-sum composite inclusions in which evaluating all components or updating all coordinates at every iteration can be computationally expensive. We develop two optimistic gradient frameworks that combine variance reduction with randomized block-coordinate updates. The first framework applies under a blockwise average Lipschitz continuity condition and the existence of a weak-Minty solution. It achieves an $\mathcal{O}(1/k)$ convergence rate for the expected squared residual, and its iterates converge almost surely under mild additional conditions. The second framework relies on a backward-forward reformulation under average co-coercivity and co-hypomonotonicity. It achieves faster $\mathcal{O}(1/k^2)$ and $o(1/k^2)$ rates for the expected squared residual, as well as $o(1/k^2)$ almost-sure rates. For both frameworks, we provide a generic condition on the stochastic estimator that covers mini-batch, loopless SVRG, and a generalized JacSketch-type estimator, and we derive the corresponding oracle complexities under importance-based block sampling. In particular, in highly heterogeneous regimes, the L-SVRG and JacSketch variants attain $\mathcal{O}\big(n + n^{2/3}\epsilon^{-2}\big)$ and $\mathcal{O}\big(n + n^{2/3}\epsilon^{-1}\big)$ oracle complexities for the nonaccelerated and accelerated methods, respectively. Numerical experiments illustrate the effects of variance reduction and block-coordinate sampling, and compare the proposed methods with existing baselines.
item.dc:creator: Ngh\~ia Nguyen-Trung, Ion Necoara, Quoc Tran-Dinh

item.title: A Note on the NP-Hardness on Quadratic Optimization over Doubly Stochastic Matrices and the Gromov-Wasserstein Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.00479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Gromov-Wasserstein problem is an extension of the regular optimal transport problem that is adapted for pairs of distributions residing in incomparable spaces. Broadly speaking, given a pair of metric measure spaces, the Gromov-Wasserstein problem seeks couplings between these spaces that minimize the distortion between the metric evaluations. In this note we record the fact that the Gromov-Wasserstein distance between finite metric spaces is NP-Hard to compute. Our argument relies on a reduction from the Hamiltonian Cycle Problem, and it builds on ideas in Vayer's thesis and Ryner et. al's work that draw connections between the 2-Gromov-Wasserstein and the Quadratic Assignment Problem. During the preparation of this manuscript we learned of the appearance of Breitung et. al's work, whose result essentially supersedes ours. We hope this note serves as a useful companion whose proof is, hopefully, more elementary and easier to understand.
item.dc:creator: Yong Sheng Soh

item.title: Constraint Qualifications and Regularity Conditions for Nonlinear Constraint Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.00526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Constraint qualifications (CQs) and regularity conditions (RCs) play a fundamental role in establishing global iteration and oracle complexity results for first-order methods on solving functional constrained optimization problems. Various conditions have been proposed and employed in the literature, with their validity established for different classes of applications. However, the use of different conditions across existing studies makes it difficult to directly compare their theoretical results and underlying assumptions. In this report, we systematically review several widely used CQs and RCs and investigate their relationships. In particular, we establish implications among these conditions and identify cases in which the implications are strict, thereby clarifying their relative strengths. Our results provide a unified perspective on existing regularity assumptions and offer guidance for selecting appropriate conditions in the complexity analysis of first-order methods.
item.dc:creator: Shiji Zuo, Qihang Lin, Wei Liu, Yangyang Xu

item.title: Dynamic programming principle for controlled systems driven by fractional Brownian motions and related backward stochastic Riccati equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.00535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work aims to study the stochastic optimal control problems of controlled stochastic differential systems driven by both Brownian motions and fractional Brownian motions via dynamic programming principle. The stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation is obtained. Different from the classical case, the obtained stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation is a backward stochastic partial differential equation driven by both fractional Brownian motions and standard Brownian motions, whose solution is a pair of random fields. For linear quadratic optimal control problem this backward stochastic partial differential equation is explicitly solved by relating it to a backward stochastic Riccati equation.
item.dc:creator: Yuecai Han, Yaozhong Hu, Yuhang Li

item.title: A Parallel Adaptive Proximal ADMM for Linearly Constrained Separable Composite Optimization Problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.00570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose and analyze an adaptive proximal alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), based on Jacobi-type updates, for linearly constrained separable nonconvex composite optimization problems. The objective consists of two block-separable functions, one continuously differentiable and weakly convex, and the other convex and Lipschitz continuous. The proposed method is adaptive to all problem parameters and allows inexact solutions of the block proximal subproblems. At each iteration, we solve all block subproblems in parallel, then apply a novel test to decide whether to update the Lagrange multiplier and/or the penalty parameter. Without any rank assumptions on the constraint matrices, we establish an ${\cal O}(\epsilon^{-3})$ iteration-complexity bound for obtaining an approximate first-order stationary point. This matches the best-known complexity for cyclic proximal ADMM methods and improves the existing complexity of Jacobi-type schemes in this general nonconvex setting. Numerical experiments on a nonconvex quadratic program illustrate the proposed method's computational benefits.
item.dc:creator: Leandro F. Maia, Renato D. C. Monteiro, Gilson N. Silva

item.title: Log-Driven Semantic Tuning for Mixed Integer Programming Solvers
item.description: arXiv:2611.00621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated configuration of mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers largely relies on black-box optimization. Each trial requires an expensive solver run and provides only a scalar outcome, so tuning can require many such evaluations. Human experts take a different approach. They inspect solver logs, identify performance bottlenecks, and adjust the parameters that address them. We propose Log-Driven Semantic Tuning (LDST), which uses a large language model (LLM) to automate this process. LDST extracts compact diagnostics from solver logs, uses the LLM to propose sparse edits to the current best configuration based on parameter meanings and observed solver behavior, and validates each proposal before execution. A regime-adaptive objective selects the tuning signal according to the information available from a time-limited run, while a log-based completion signal estimates completion time from branch-and-bound tree growth recorded in ordinary solver logs, so that solved and unsolved runs share one time scale. On 215 instances from five benchmark sets, LDST reduces geometric-mean loss by 43.9% on easy instances and 16.7% on intermediate instances relative to the best of SMAC3, RBFOpt, and random search. In both regimes, LDST achieves a lower loss with 10 proposals than any of these baselines achieves with 50. Configurations that LDST tunes on a single instance also transfer better than baseline configurations to unseen instances of the same family.
item.dc:creator: Zhengzhong Ricky You, Kaizhao Sun, Zeping Min, Wotao Yin, Xinshang Wang

item.title: ALDER: A Single-Loop Augmented-Lagrangian Damped Extragradient Method for Nonconvex--Concave Minimax Problems with Nonlinear Coupled Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.00691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: ALDER, a single-loop augmented-Lagrangian damped extragradient method, is proposed for smooth nonconvex--concave minimax problems with nonlinear coupled inequality constraints. Within an augmented-Lagrangian framework, ALDER combines prediction--correction steps for the primal variables with explicit projected-and-relaxed multiplier updates in a single loop. The penalty parameter is fixed throughout each run, eliminating inner-loop subproblem solves and iterative penalty updates. We establish uniform boundedness of the relaxed multiplier sequence and, under an extended Mangasarian--Fromovitz constraint qualification, boundedness of the projected output multiplier. Building on these bounds, we show that ALDER finds an $\varepsilon$-KKT point within $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-7/2})$ complete first-order oracle evaluations in the strongly concave setting and $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ in the concave setting. These bounds improve upon the best known complexity bounds for multi-loop algorithms for this problem class, achieved by FAL, by removing a $\log(1/\varepsilon)$ factor, while retaining a single-loop update structure.
item.dc:creator: H. Zhang, M. Zhang, Z. Xu, Y. -H. Dai

item.title: Forgetting matters: when subspace optimization accelerates without the strong convexity parameter
item.description: arXiv:2611.00727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sequential subspace optimization (SESOP) minimizes the objective exactly over a few directions built from past iterates. It needs no problem constants, is accelerated on smooth convex functions and behaves like an accelerated method in experiments. This led to the conjecture that it is accelerated in the strongly convex case without knowing the strong convexity parameter. We show that the conjecture fails in the worst case. For every subspace method whose memory forgets slowly, namely a window of recent gradients and steps together with cumulative sums with subexponential weights, we construct a counterexample: acceleration requires a window of length of order $\sqrt{\kappa}$, where $\kappa$ is the condition number. SESOP and the plane form of conjugate gradients are therefore not accelerated. Memories that forget fast avoid this obstruction. Pairs of geometric filters give accelerated methods with logarithmic memory or only two stored vectors. They need neither the strong convexity parameter nor the smoothness constant, never restart the iterate and restart their memory at most $O(\log\kappa)$ times. Finally, the method with fixed activation times remains asymptotically accelerated on functions with Lipschitz Hessian even when each subproblem is solved by a single Newton step.
item.dc:creator: Ilya Kuruzov, Alexander Vyguzov, Ivan Dorofeev, Alexander Gasnikov

item.title: Maximum principle for discrete-time stochastic recursive games driven by fractional noises
item.description: arXiv:2611.00740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates discrete-time stochastic recursive games driven by fractional noises, in which the cost functional is defined through a backward stochastic difference equation. By introducing discrete-time adjoint equations, we establish a maximum principle and the verification theorem for open-loop Nash equilibria in non-zero sum and zero sum stochastic recursive game problems. The effectiveness of our theorem is demonstrated through applications to two different linear-quadratic stochastic recursive games and a portfolio selection problem with a recursive utility functional.
item.dc:creator: Yuecai Han, Yuhang Li, Chenfei Wang

item.title: Agent4FreeFem: A Verification-Guided Framework for Autonomous Topology Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.00803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topology optimization has become an indispensable design tool in the aerospace, automotive, and mechanical engineering industries. Yet bringing a new problem from its description to an optimized result remains slow, expert-dependent, and unreliable: the workflow spans many manually connected stages, each new problem requires solver code to be written and debugged manually, and such code often fails or yields incorrect results. We present Agent4FreeFem, a pipeline driven by a large language model that turns a natural-language problem description into a set of verified optimization results without manual solver-code development or debugging. The pipeline keeps the problem definition unmodified, localizes errors using independent sources of evidence, and completes constrained repairs automatically, thereby providing efficient end-to-end automation, autonomous execution, and verifiable results. We evaluated Agent4FreeFem on a suite of single-physics and coupled multiphysics problems. Every case passed runtime verification and finished within the repair budget of each stage.
item.dc:creator: Zhipu Cui, Helin Gong, Shengfeng Zhu

item.title: When are dividend barriers optimal? A distributional characterization in renewal risk models
item.description: arXiv:2611.00827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the finite-horizon optimal dividend problem in a renewal risk model with unrestricted dividend payments, examining how claim-size distributions determine barrier optimality. Under general assumptions on a fixed interclaim-time distribution, we prove that exponential claims admit a globally optimal barrier for every positive safety loading, positive discount rate and finite horizon. Conversely, within the class of claim-size distributions with continuous nondecreasing hazard, every nonexponential law admits one fixed premium--discount pair for which no barrier is globally optimal at any sufficiently long horizon. These results establish, within this distribution class, an equivalence between exponentially distributed claims and the existence of a globally optimal barrier for every parameter combination in the stated range. Numerical examples compare exponential and Gamma claims with the same mean and illustrate how the claim-size distribution changes the structure of dividend decisions.
item.dc:creator: Linyu Miao

item.title: A Telescopic Method with Guaranteed B-Stationarity for Partitioned Cardinality and Complementarity Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.00897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the minimization of a smooth function subject to box constraints and partitioned cardinality constraints (PCC): the variables are divided into groups and, within each group, at most a prescribed number of variables may be non-zero. This class contains bound-constrained minimization, cardinality-constrained minimization and bound-constrained mathematical programs with complementarity constraints. We introduce the Telescopic Method, which alternates iterations of a bound-constrained method on the faces of the feasible set with inexpensive one-dimensional "escaping" tests that exchange a variable of the current face by a currently null one within the same group. We prove, without constraint qualifications and without requiring global solutions of subproblems, that every limit point of the generated sequence is B-stationary, i.e., it satisfies the first-order condition defined by the tangent cone of the feasible set. This guarantee is obtained with exchanges of a single variable, whatever the number of non-null entries of the limit point, because B-stationarity for this class of problems decomposes into conditions on single variables. On the 60 bound-constrained mathematical programs with complementarity constraints of the test set of Kirches, Larson, Leyffer and Manns, the method found approximately B-stationary points in all the problems. Applications to separable regression, sparse polynomial approximation and portfolio selection are described and tested numerically.
item.dc:creator: Ernesto G. Birgin, J. M. Mart\'inez

item.title: Consumption and Investment with Multiple Job-Switching Opportunities
item.description: arXiv:2611.00900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite-horizon optimal switching with affine rewards in a consumption-investment model with finitely many occupational regimes. Directed shortest-path costs yield the exact natural borrowing limit. A dual transformation reduces the control problem to a one-dimensional system of variational inequalities with interconnected obstacles. Convexity and a distributional waiting inequality give local spatial $C^{1,1}$ regularity and smooth fit, including destination ties. These estimates establish strong duality and recover optimal consumption, investment, and switching strategies. A reflected backward stochastic differential equation representation yields a set-based integral formula without prescribed boundary geometry. Every connected component of the spatially regular locus is a maximal smooth graph over time. Exact examples exhibit disconnected contact sets, temporal boundaries under strict triangle costs, and a corner in an individual boundary component under additive route costs. A convergent time discretisation completes the analysis.
item.dc:creator: Gugyum Ha, Junkee Jeon

item.title: Euler discretizations, invariant faces and brackets for lower exponents of positive switched systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.00901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that explicit and implicit Euler discretizations yield monotone brackets for the lower Lyapunov exponent of positive switched systems. We establish convergence of the implicit bound for every Metzler family. For the explicit bound, we derive convergence criteria in reducible systems from a face formula for the uniform lower exponent on an invariant cone. The formula takes the minimum of the rates on faces that meet the cone nontrivially and are preserved by at least one mode, using only their preserving modes. For individually irreducible modes, we prove O(h) discretization errors, where h is the step size, and show that this order is sharp in general. At interior two-mode chattering optima with an irreducible optimal mixture, we obtain one-sided first-order bounds. We also construct a three-mode example in which the explicit bound converges while finite polytope lower bounds remain capped strictly below the true exponent. We prove convergence of fixed-antinorm Gripenberg brackets under individual irreducibility as the step and tolerance decrease and the search depth increases appropriately. Finally, we obtain independently verified continuous-time brackets by exact rational checks, with lower bounds that remain valid at smaller steps.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Paolo Maiale

item.title: Quantum-Inspired Hamiltonian Descent for Radiation Therapy Treatment Planning
item.description: arXiv:2611.00989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Direct incorporation of dose-volume constraints into inverse radiotherapy planning leads to large mixed-integer optimization problems that accurately represent clinical requirements but are computationally challenging. We develop and evaluate a quantum-inspired approach for automated dose-volume-constrained intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) and intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) planning. Clinical requirements are formulated as mixed-integer optimization problems, with binary variables representing dose-volume constraint violations. Patient-specific dose-influence matrices are generated at the photon control-point and proton spot levels, and intensities are optimized using Quantum-Inspired Hamiltonian Descent (QIHD). We evaluate QIHD on eight clinical cases: four IMRT (two prostate, one head-and-neck, and one liver) and four IMPT (two lung, one prostate, and one liver). The IMRT formulations contain 27,621 to 112,565 variables and are solved in 5 to 32 minutes, while the IMPT formulations contain 69,861 to 221,342 variables and are solved in 11 to 35 minutes on an NVIDIA RTX 4060 GPU. QIHD produces dose distributions satisfying clinical protocols without manual intervention. In comparison, a CPU implementation of Gurobi fails to solve most tested mixed-integer formulations within several hours. These results demonstrate the computational feasibility of GPU-accelerated QIHD for automated photon and proton treatment planning. Prospective clinical validation and implementation of decomposed subproblems on quantum hardware remain future directions.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadhossein Mohammadisiahroydi, Yuxiang Peng, Jiaqi Leng, Robabeh Rahimi, Arezoo Modiri, Wei Zou, Tamas Terlaky, Xiaodi Wu

item.title: Finite-Time Tracking Success or Failure in the Pursuer--Evader Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.01054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a sufficient framework for determining the success or failure of finite-time tracking in pursuer--evader dynamics. To this end, we design a nonsmooth coupled multi-agent system by adopting a previously established pursuer--evader model from the existing literature, which characterizes asymptotic tracking success and failure, as the backbone. We then provide appropriate sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of initial data, system parameters, and kernel functionals, under which some pursuers can successfully track evaders within a finite time, while others fail to do so. In particular, we show that the pursuer--evader subsystem associated with the pursuers that successfully track the evader, together with the corresponding evaders, exhibits finite-time stability.
item.dc:creator: Woojoo Shim, Hyunjin Ahn

item.title: Robust Optimization in Stochastic Games
item.description: arXiv:2611.01151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A player's impatient valuation of an infinite stream of stage payoffs is a weighted average with nonincreasing weights. Such valuations generalize geometric discounting and allow imprecise or heterogeneous time preferences. For a stochastic game \(\Gamma\) and a profile \(u\) of impatient valuations, let \(\Gamma_u\) be the induced game. We ask when approximately optimal or equilibrium behavior can be chosen to vary continuously and stably with \(u\). We show that this robustness is governed by the corresponding uniform long-run payoff property: the uniform value in the adversary case, and uniform approximate equilibrium payoffs in the equilibrium case. In finite state spaces, the latter is equivalent to the usual existence of a uniform equilibrium payoff. In the two-player zero-sum case, if \(\Gamma\) has a uniform value, then the value of \(\Gamma_u\) varies uniformly continuously with \(u\), and for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a uniformly continuous mapping assigning to each \(u\) an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal strategy in \(\Gamma_u\). Hence this holds for every finite two-player zero-sum stochastic game. In the non-zero-sum case, uniform approximate equilibrium payoffs imply a finite cover of the valuation-profile space by neighborhoods on each of which a single strategy profile is a robust \(\varepsilon\)-equilibrium. For sunspot, correlated, and extensive-form correlated equilibria, uniform approximate equilibrium payoffs are equivalent to the existence, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), of a uniformly continuous mapping assigning to each valuation profile a robust \(\varepsilon\)-equilibrium on a neighborhood of that profile. Consequently, every finite stochastic game admits uniformly continuous robust extensive-form correlated \(\varepsilon\)-equilibrium selections.
item.dc:creator: Abraham Neyman

item.title: Entropic Column Generation and Lehmer Branch-and-Price for Bin Packing Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.01251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Lehmer branch-and-price, an exact algorithm for bin packing and cutting stock problems built on the Lehmer transform, the ratio of Mellin transforms of item weights at consecutive orders. The transform maps each bin, a finite multiset of item weights, to a smooth increasing curve, and so gives the discrete problem a continuous representation on which the tools of analysis, such as convexity, exponential families and smoothing, can act. Read along this curve, the problem yields an explicit dual solution, a monotone representation of the dominance order, a family of constructive heuristics with first fit decreasing as its limit, and an integer identity that tells when the linear relaxation can decide an instance and when only a perfect packing can improve the best solution known. Lifted from items to patterns, the transform gives entropic column generation, a new form of column generation that bounds the relaxation from both sides at every iteration without solving the pricing problem exactly, maximizes a smoothed dual at an explicit rate, and measures by an entropy how much the relaxation leaves undecided. We show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on the standard benchmark in both the number of instances solved and the computational time.
item.dc:creator: Masoud Ataei

item.title: Singular Perturbations for Control Systems Safety
item.description: arXiv:2611.01266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) offer a powerful theory for enforcing safety in dynamical systems. Yet, applying this framework to complex systems is challenging when subsystems are feedback-interconnected and operate at different timescales. Such structures arise naturally in multiphysics systems and in control architectures where physical plants interact with optimization, estimation, and control algorithms. In many of these settings, safety involves only part of the system, motivating the design of reduced-order certificates. Inspired by singular perturbation theory, we establish sufficient conditions, involving separation between slow and fast dynamics, under which a reduced-order safety certificate can be lifted to the full interconnected system. Specifically, we construct a composite CBF ensuring forward invariance of a lifted subset of the original safe set. We also show that the certified safe set expands monotonically as the tuning parameter accelerating the fast dynamics is reduced. Numerical results validate the approach on two robotic systems: a planar 2-DoF manipulator with motor dynamics and a 6-DoF UR10e manipulator controlled by a suboptimal optimization algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Di Gregorio, Guido Carnevale, Giuseppe Notarstefano

item.title: Mixed-Integer Programming for Causal Discovery with Unknown Hard-Intervention Targets
item.description: arXiv:2611.01267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When intervention targets are uncertain, learning causal relationships and identifying directly perturbed variables become a joint task. We develop an exact mixed-integer program based on optimized parent-set scores (PS-MIP) for joint graph and intervention-target estimation in linear Gaussian structural equation models under stochastic hard interventions. The method can incorporate candidate-edge restrictions and partial target knowledge when available. For each random variable, PS-MIP evaluates candidate sets of direct causes, or parent sets, by optimizing the likelihood parameters and compatible target patterns, retaining both the score and a minimizing target pattern. A global mixed-integer program then selects parent sets subject to acyclicity. Under stated conditions, this reduction preserves the joint objective and reconstructs the graph, targets, and likelihood parameters. Because the local scores are precomputed, PS-MIP replaces a direct large bilinear mixed-integer program with a linear selection problem; empirically it certifies global optimality on far more instances than the direct formulation (126 of 180 versus 34) and is often orders of magnitude faster. On synthetic data, PS-MIP achieves favorable false-discovery--true-discovery trade-offs relative to several benchmark algorithms for causal discovery with unknown intervention targets, along with strong intervention-target recovery in denser settings. An exploratory study on real data from a controlled physical system further demonstrates recovery beyond simulation.
item.dc:creator: Tong Xu, Armeen Taeb, Simge K\"u\c{c}\"ukyavuz, Ali Shojaie

item.title: Differentially Private Distributed Optimization via the Intrinsic Randomness of Zeroth-Order Estimators: Sampling Geometry, Convergence, and Privacy Guarantees
item.description: arXiv:2611.01373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed zeroth-order optimization has gained increasing attention in applications where exact gradients are computationally expensive or unavailable. However, the iterative exchange of local decision variables makes distributed networks vulnerable to inference attacks. While differential privacy provides a rigorous framework for privacy protection, conventional approaches generally require additional random noise, which inevitably affects optimization accuracy. In this paper, we investigate whether the randomness inherent in zeroth-order estimation can itself provide privacy protection. We develop a distributed zeroth-order gradient descent method that integrates consensus updates with a ball-uniform two-point gradient estimator. Our theoretical analysis shows that our algorithm attains standard convergence guarantees in both online and offline optimization settings. We then characterize the relevant probability distributions of the associated privacy mechanism, and establish differential privacy guarantees for both the online and offline optimization settings. These results reveal the potential of intrinsic zeroth-order randomness for privacy protection.
item.dc:creator: Jiajun Wang, Yujie Tang

item.title: Benign population landscapes do not transfer to empirical risk minimization in nonsmooth optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.01384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Benign landscapes provide a geometric explanation for the success of iterative methods on nonconvex problems arising in data science. The landscape is benign if every local minimizer is global and every other critical point is a strict saddle. For methods that avoid strict saddles, convergence to a critical point therefore implies convergence to a global minimizer. For smooth stochastic optimization, a common strategy for establishing such landscapes proceeds in two steps: $(i)$ establish benign geometry for the population objective---which is often easier to analyze---and $(ii)$ transfer this geometry to the empirical objective using concentration of gradients and Hessians. Recent work has extended saddle-point avoidance guarantees to weakly convex nonsmooth optimization through the notion of active strict saddles. We show, however, that benign population geometry need not transfer to empirical objectives in this setting. Specifically, for robust phase retrieval with Gaussian measurements---a well-studied and highly structured problem---the population objective is benign. Nevertheless, the empirical objective has sharp spurious local minima with probability bounded away from zero as the sample size tends to infinity. This asymptotic probability lower bound is independent of the dimension.
item.dc:creator: Penghao Wang, Mateo D\'iaz, Liwei Jiang

item.title: Three-phase time minimization transportation problem with non-idle phases: a polynomial two-witness algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2611.01387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The three-phase time minimization transportation problem partitions the origin-terminal links into three sets used in consecutive phases and minimizes the sum of the phase shipment times. Optimal solutions may leave a phase idle, as in the main example of the original study. We require every phase to carry a positive integer quantity while leaving the split of the total requirement across phases free. Discarding idle solutions from the original algorithm does not, in general, solve this variant. We prove that the optimum is attained by fixing one witness link in each of two phases and deciding the third phase by a single network flow computation, with the optimal Phase-3 time of each witness pair located by binary search. The resulting exact algorithm is strongly polynomial. It extends to any fixed number of phases, whereas, when the number of phases is part of the input, even non-idle feasibility is strongly NP-complete; feasibility alone is fixed-parameter tractable in the number of phases via known rainbow-matching results. We also characterize the minimum time of each phase. On the main example, non-idleness raises the optimum from 38 to 41. On 3,650 random instances with up to $50\times50$ links the algorithm took at most 50.2 seconds, and non-idleness raised the optimal value in 41% of the 2,250 instances with equal phase sizes; on 90 sampled instances it was faster than a mixed integer programming solver on 80 with a direct formulation and on 65 with a tighter threshold formulation.
item.dc:creator: Sailesh Kamalahasan, Raghav Paladugu, Archana Khurana

item.title: Longest-Queue Policies in Dynamic Matching with Abandonments
item.description: arXiv:2611.01431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a dynamic two-way matching market in which agents of heterogeneous types arrive over time, wait to be matched according to a compatibility network, and abandon the system if their random patience expires. The decision maker collects match rewards and pays holding and abandonment costs, and seeks to maximize the expected net value over a finite horizon. We evaluate policies by their approximation ratio against a fluid benchmark, the optimal value of a linear-programming relaxation that upper bounds the expected net value of every policy. Under a general position gap (GPG) condition, which requires the unique optimal dual solution of this linear program to remain optimal under small perturbations of the arrival rates, we propose a longest-queue policy. The policy first uses this dual solution to identify a set of good match types and a set of critical agent types. Upon each arrival, it considers only good matches and matches the arrival to the critical partner with the longest queue subject to availabilities. In the high-volume regime, in which arrival rates are scaled by s, we prove that the policy attains an approximation ratio of at least 1-O(1/s) at every scale s >= 1 and every horizon T >= 1, so the ratio tends to 1 as s goes to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Siqi He, Yehua Wei, Jiaming Xu

item.title: Robust Appointment Scheduling with Heterogeneous Costs
item.description: arXiv:2611.01478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing simple appointment systems that under uncertainty in service times, try to achieve both high utilization of expensive medical equipment and personnel as well as short waiting time for patients, has long been an interesting and challenging problem in health care. We consider a robust version of the appointment scheduling problem, introduced by Mittal et al.\ (2014), with the goal of finding simple and easy-to-use algorithms. Previous work focused on the special case where per-unit costs due to under-utilization of equipment/personnel are homogeneous i.e., costs are linear and identical. We consider the heterogeneous case and devise an LP that has a simple closed-form solution. This solution yields the first constant-factor approximation for the problem. We also find special cases beyond homogeneous costs where the LP leads to closed form optimal schedules. Our approach and results extend more generally to convex piece-wise linear costs. For the case where the order of patients is changeable, we focus on linear costs and show that the problem is strongly NP-hard when the under-utilization costs are heterogeneous. For changeable order with homogeneous under-utilization costs, it was previously shown that an EPTAS exists. We instead find an extremely simple, ratio-based ordering that is 1.0604 approximate.
item.dc:creator: Andreas S. Schulz, Rajan Udwani

item.title: Variance Reduction Note 3: The Convergence of PAGE
item.description: arXiv:2611.01523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The probabilistic gradient estimator (PAGE) alternates randomly between an accurate gradient refresh and a cheap recursive correction. This third expository note on recursive variance reduction explains the algorithm and gives a self-contained convergence proof for smooth nonconvex optimization. A Lyapunov function combines objective decrease with estimation error, turning the refresh probability into an explicit contraction parameter. The resulting expected oracle complexity is $O(n+\sqrt n\,\epsilon^{-2})$ for finite sums and $O(\epsilon^{-3})$ for online problems, with the other problem parameters fixed. Initialization, refreshes, and both evaluations in each gradient difference are counted. The presentation is pedagogical and makes no claim of a new algorithm or convergence rate.
item.dc:creator: Alina Lodhi

item.title: Strong convergence of a slowly damped primal-dual dynamical system with general time-scaling, Tikhonov regularization and implicit Hessian damping
item.description: arXiv:2611.01538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a novel mixed-order inertial primal-dual dynamical system with general time-scaling and Tikhonov regularization coefficients, together with implicit Hessian damping, for solving convex optimization problems with linear equality constraints in Hilbert spaces. The proposed dynamical system incorporates slowly vanishing viscous damping and is developed based on a time-dependent Tikhonov-regularized Lagrangian. Under suitable assumptions, we establish fast convergence rates for the objective residual, the feasibility violation, and the primal-dual gap using a Lyapunov analysis. Moreover, we prove that the generated primal-dual trajectory converges strongly to the minimum-norm primal-dual solution. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results and indicate improved convergence performance relative to the comparison dynamical systems.
item.dc:creator: Yixuan Ma, Honglu Li, Yibin Xiao

item.title: Distributionally Robust Optimization over Incomparable Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) provides a principled framework for making decisions under uncertainty when the underlying distribution may be incorrectly specified. A widely used approach builds on ideas from optimal transport (OT) as a means of measuring differences between distributions. However, this depends on these distributions residing in the same space. In certain settings, the reference data distribution we have and the space on which we make our decision may be different, which renders classical OT techniques impossible. In this paper, we provide a new DRO formulation in which ambiguity sets are defined through the Gromov-Wasserstein distance, which is an extension of OT to pairs of distributions residing in incomparable spaces. We show that several seemingly unrelated optimization formulations, including conditional value-at-risk minimization, group distributionally robust optimization, robust graph $k$-median, and $k$-median with outliers, can be recovered as special cases of our formulation. We describe the computational aspects of solving the proposed formulation based on the doubly-nonnegative relaxation. Last, we illustrate the framework through experiments on clustering over incomparable spaces and stochastic graph $k$-median.
item.dc:creator: Junyu Chen, Jieling Shi, Yong Sheng Soh

item.title: Smoothed analysis of stability radii for the assignment problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.01584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every linear program can tolerate small changes to its costs and still yield a solution of the original problem. The size of this tolerance measures how robust an optimal decision is to noise or numerical error, and how much regularization the problem can support. Classical sensitivity analysis can determine this tolerance only from an optimal solution. This paper provides a priori lower bounds on two measures of this tolerance -- the optimality gap and the $\infty$-norm stability radius -- for the $n$-by-$n$ linear assignment problem over the Birkhoff polytope. The bounds derive from a smoothed analysis, which adds Gaussian noise with standard deviation of at least $\sigma$ in every direction to an arbitrary base cost. At every fixed confidence level, uniformly over the base cost, both quantities are at least of order $\sigma/(n\sqrt{\log n})$. The radius bound is asymptotically sharp. Under isotropic noise, the worst case occurs when every assignment has equal cost, and in this case, a scaled stability radius converges in distribution to a standard exponential variable.
item.dc:creator: Michael P. Friedlander

item.title: OCP-Based Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Quadrotor Trajectory Tracking
item.description: arXiv:2611.01628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fast online optimization is essential for nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) on resource-limited aerial platforms. This paper presents an analytical-derivative NMPC solver for quadrotor trajectory tracking. For the state-affine translational model with held thrust and attitude commands, fourth-order Runge--Kutta integration yields an exact discrete-time prediction map. Forward--backward difference equations provide the gradient and exact Hessian of the finite-horizon cost condensed over the input sequence. These derivatives drive a nested optimal-control-based direction recursion, while a shifted warm start reuses the preceding solution. The resulting solver addresses the unconstrained tracking problem without a general-purpose nonlinear programming package. Gazebo experiments show comparable tracking accuracy to iLQR and two acados SQP configurations, with mean solver-time speedups of $1.97$--$2.30$. In onboard flight tests, the mean solver time is $0.3121$\,ms, corresponding to speedups of $3.37$--$5.77$ over the same baselines. The largest measured solver time is $3.7754$\,ms within a $20$-ms control period. These measurements cover the numerical solver and exclude estimation, communication, and command publication.
item.dc:creator: Lv Shichao, Lv Chuanzhi, Wang Hongxia, Huanshui Zhang

item.title: Long-Time Behavior of Zero-Noise Mean-Field Adam
item.description: arXiv:2611.01658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive methods such as Adam are the most commonly used methods for training neural networks, but their long-time behavior is not as well understood as that of non-adaptive methods. This is particularly true in the mean-field limit, where the dynamics of infinitely many neurons are described as a distribution over parameters which satisfies a self-consistency condition. In this paper, we study a deterministic continuous-time model of Adam in the mean-field setting. Under a condition relating the averaging rates of the momentum and second-moment variables, the size of the gradients, and a regularization parameter, we prove that the distribution of parameters converges to the set of equilibria. This condition extends the range known for finite-dimensional models, and we show that it is sharp. Under an additional Lojasiewicz-type inequality for distributions, we prove that individual parameter trajectories converge and obtain quantitative rates for this convergence. We verify the qualitative convergence assumptions for a regularized two-layer neural network. We also show that adding noise to the momentum prevents the system from approaching these equilibria and rules out many free-energy type Lyapunov functionals. Finally, numerical experiments illustrate the energy estimates, give evidence of persistent oscillations outside the sufficient parameter range, and compare the observed decay with the predicted rates.
item.dc:creator: Ethan Huffman, Asaf Cohen

item.title: Multirate Data-Driven Predictive Control: Rank Obstructions, Identifiability, and Noise Conditioning
item.description: arXiv:2611.01665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop rank, identifiability, and noise-conditioning results for compact input--output predictors in multirate data-driven predictive control. The inverse of a square zero-input response matrix used in an existing compact-lifting construction is shown to be undefined under its observability and minimal-polynomial assumptions. We derive exact replacements using rank-complete data, characterize all predictor extensions, and establish the minimum-norm and minimax Euclidean noise properties of the canonical Moore--Penrose extension. A joint predictor is identified directly from mixed experiments with arbitrary initial states. Deterministic perturbation bounds quantify reconstruction errors through informative singular-value margins, while a positive-definite reduced weighting preserves the nominal quadratic cost. Sampling-rate observability and event-triggering analyses identify additional conditions needed for reconstruction and stability guarantees.
item.dc:creator: Robert Vrabel

item.title: Singular Tracking of Fractional Brownian Motion under Proportional Costs
item.description: arXiv:2611.01727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study adapted finite-variation tracking of fractional Brownian motion under quadratic loss and proportional adjustment costs. For $H\in(0,1)$, \[ V_\lambda(T;a,b,\sigma)\underset{\lambda\downarrow0}{\sim}\kappa_HT a^{(1-H)/(1+H)}(\lambda b)^{2H/(1+H)}\sigma^{2/(1+H)}. \] The positive long-run cell value $\kappa_H$ is unchanged by full past information. A bounded full-past reset correction yields finite-horizon bounds and continuity in $H$. The Brownian value is $\kappa_{1/2}=\frac12(\frac32)^{2/3}$. Coupling local paths with their filtrations gives a local limit, which we verify for Gaussian Volterra targets. Every asymptotically optimal control has the same leading tracking--variation cost split. Primal and dual bounds quantify the cell value. For $H<1/2$, we construct a positive-factor approximation and relate factor resolution to horizon length.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Autran

item.title: Expected Minimax Regret Rates for Adaptive LQG Control on Fixed Parameter Sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.01739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how a fixed model family determines expected minimax regret in adaptive LQG control. The family is compact and affine, with partial observation and unknown noise covariances. We quantify how information from residual covariances and input responses can vanish relative to differences between optimal control laws. This relation yields matching bounds that classify regret as bounded, logarithmic, sublinear polynomial or linear. Polynomial exponents are rational. For real algebraic model and cost data, a terminating procedure determines the regret class and the exact exponent of polynomial growth before data collection. A causal policy attains these rates using model estimation and bounded probes, reselecting model sets from observations without a supplied common stabilizer. For costs with fixed positive definite output and input weights, polynomial exponents are at most one half.
item.dc:creator: Zhaobo Liu

item.title: The maximum concentration of results in incomplete round-robin tournaments
item.description: arXiv:2611.01750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Herfindahl--Hirschman Index (HHI), a standard measure of market concentration, is widely used to quantify competitive balance in sports tournaments. To enable comparisons over time or across leagues, both its minimum and maximum should be known. The minimum is usually trivial. Our paper provides results on the maximum HHI in incomplete round-robin tournaments, where the set of matches is represented by a regular but not complete undirected graph. We prove that the lower bound of maximum HHI is reached when the tournament consists of independent round-robin groups, while the upper bound of maximum HHI is reached when the set of matches is represented by a bipartite graph. Maximising HHI is computationally difficult even for highly structured graph types corresponding to real-world tournaments, where the teams are partitioned into pots and play the same number of matches against opponents from every pot. The complexity of the problem does not depend on the scoring system or the number of opponents from a pot.
item.dc:creator: Gergely Cs\'aji, L\'aszl\'o Csat\'o

item.title: Optimization Frameworks & Learning Algorithms for Discrete-Time Mean Field Games
item.description: arXiv:2611.01754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This monograph introduces discrete-time mean field games with finite state and action spaces, emphasizing optimization formulations and learning algorithms. Starting from Markov decision processes and finite-player stochastic games, it develops the notion of mean field Nash equilibrium, establishes existence and uniqueness results under suitable assumptions, and explains how mean field equilibria yield approximate equilibria in large finite-player games. Building on the linear programming formulation of Markov decision processes, occupation measures and primal-dual formulations connect equilibrium computation with mathematical optimization. The monograph presents fixed-point iterations, fictitious play, online mirror descent, and optimization-based methods, discussing their convergence properties and limitations. Numerical examples illustrate crowd motion, traffic routing, epidemic management, and the computation of multiple equilibria. It combines examples, theoretical results, and implementable algorithms, with bibliographic notes providing connections to the broader literature.
item.dc:creator: Xin Guo, Mathieu Lauri\`ere

item.title: Multi-rate high-order regularization with an order-$(p-2)$ oracle
item.description:
arXiv:2611.01819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider unconstrained minimization of a possibly nonconvex function $f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}$ whose $p$th derivative is Lipschitz continuous, with $p\geq3$, when derivative information is available only through order $p-2$. The unavailable tensors $
abla^{p-1}f$ and $
abla^pf$ are reconstructed from central finite differences of $
abla^{p-2}f$. Since the two reconstructions have different point-query costs, we use a block length $m$ for the order-$p$ approximation and a subblock length $\ell\leq m$ for the order-$(p-1)$ approximation. The latter is transported between consecutive reconstruction points using the stored order-$p$ approximation. This leads to an adaptive regularization method that does not require prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant. We prove finite termination at an $\epsilon$-approximate first-order stationary point and derive an explicit bound on the number of bundled order-$(p-2)$ oracle queries. For $m=(p-2)n^2$ and $\ell=(p-2)n$, the accuracy-dependent term has dimension--accuracy scaling $n^{3/p}\epsilon^{-(p+1)/p}$. Thus the method retains the $\epsilon^{-(p+1)/p}$ dependence of full order-$p$ regularization while using derivatives only through order $p-2$. Within the dense reconstruction framework considered here, using separate block and subblock lengths gives dimension dependence of order $n^{3/p}$, compared with $n^{4/p}$ when a common length is imposed.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Kabgani

item.title: On Exact Dual and Mixed-Integer Reformulations for Finite Horizon Markov Decision Processes with Submodular Revenue Maximization
item.description: arXiv:2611.01863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study exact mixed-integer reformulations of a finite horizon Markov decision process (MDP) with transition revenues defined by local submodular revenue maximization problems. We start with the dual linear programming formulation of the MDP, where local optimal revenues appear in the objective function and the constraints describe the state probabilities from the initial state. We combine the dual formulation with the binary variables of the local problems and obtain an exact mixed-integer nonlinear formulation with bilinear terms. We use the submodular inequalities and an exact McCormick linearization to obtain an equivalent mixed-integer linear formulation. We also use the dual structure to conduct a sensitivity analysis of the MDP optimal value with respect to changes in the local revenue coefficients. Based on local incumbent revenues and upper bounds, this sensitivity analysis evaluates the effect of local optimality gaps on the global MDP optimality gap, without solving every local revenue maximization problem to optimality.
item.dc:creator: Jia-Yu Chen, Hsin-Yuan Huang, Tzu-Yang Teng, Yun-Jen Tsai, Hao-Hsiang Wu

item.title: Recent Developments in HPR Methods for Large-Scale Linear Programming
item.description: arXiv:2611.01872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present recent developments in Halpern Peaceman-Rachford (HPR) methods for solving large-scale linear programming problems. We first introduce the semi-proximal HPR framework and summarize its convergence guarantees, together with its connections to Halpern PDHG and ergodic Peaceman-Rachford iterations. To improve practical performance, we develop adaptive restart and penalty parameter update strategies. We then describe several computational enhancements, including GPU-based preprocessing, diagonal scaling, reusable execution plans for sparse matrix-vector multiplication, and sieving techniques. We further discuss multi-GPU parallelization and lossless model storage and loading for handling large-scale instances. These developments form the foundation of HPR-LP, a GPU-accelerated solver for large-scale linear programming.
item.dc:creator: Kaihuang Chen, Qilin Lai, Yijia Liang, Jiawei Lu, Defeng Sun, Yancheng Yuan, Guojun Zhang, Xiangyu Zhang, Xinyuan Zhao

item.title: Recent Developments in HPR Methods for Large-Scale Convex Composite Quadratic Programming
item.description: arXiv:2611.01887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present recent developments in Halpern Peaceman--Rachford (HPR) methods for solving large-scale convex composite quadratic programming problems. Within a unified HPR framework applied to the restricted Wolfe dual, we develop several algorithmic variants based on different choices of the semi-proximal operator $\mathcal{T}_1$ for the joint dual subproblem. Specifically, an sGS-based construction leads to a sequential $w$--$y$--$w$ update scheme, while a block-linearized construction eliminates cross-block coupling and enables parallel dual updates. To improve the latter, we further introduce a coupling-aware construction that exploits a second spectral moment to obtain a tighter row majorizer. We extend the framework to convex quadratically constrained quadratic programming through factor-based second-order cone reformulations. Additional computational enhancements include equality Gram scaling and asynchronous CPU polishing. We establish convergence results under fixed metrics and discuss practical adaptive strategies.
item.dc:creator: Kaihuang Chen, Defeng Sun, Yancheng Yuan, Guojun Zhang, Xinyuan Zhao

item.title: Convergence Guarantees for the Broximal Point Method under Perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2611.01933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Broximal Point Method (BPM) of Gruntkowska et al. (2025) comes with strong guarantees for convex optimization: under convexity alone, it terminates after finitely many steps and converges linearly in function value, with bounds that do not depend on the condition number or on any other regularity property of the objective. Each iteration, however, requires the exact minimization of the objective over a ball, which is generally intractable. As a first step toward implementable variants, we study the method when these subproblems are solved only approximately. We introduce and analyze Inexact BPM, which replaces the exact broximal point by an approximation and makes no assumption on how this approximation is obtained. Under summable or sufficiently small errors, we bound the number of iterations needed to reach a neighborhood of the set of minimizers, and these bounds remain independent of the regularity of the objective. Under the weaker requirement that the errors stay below the ball radius, we prove sublinear convergence in function value for the exact broximal points underlying the perturbed iterates, valid until the target neighborhood is reached, and we recover linear rates under bounded sublevel sets or strong convexity.
item.dc:creator: Alina Abdikarimova, Ammar Mahran, Peter Richt\'arik

item.title: Multi-Period Donation Allocation for Food Banks under Stochastic Capacity and Supply
item.description: arXiv:2611.01947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Each food bank within the national Feeding America network faces the challenge of distributing donated food equitably across the food-insecure population it serves while minimizing food storage and waste over a multi-period planning horizon. Donated food supply is highly stochastic, and distribution to beneficiaries is done by autonomous local agencies whose capacities are uncertain and vary over time. Based on our long-standing partnership with a regional food bank in the southeastern United States, we address the equitable and effective distribution of food donations to charitable agencies over a finite planning horizon under uncertain capacity and supply. We derive structural properties of this problem and use them to develop efficient heuristics. An extensive numerical study evaluates the performance of the heuristics relative to a stochastic dynamic programming benchmark, which suffers from the curse of dimensionality. One heuristic consistently provides near-optimal solutions and can be easily implemented by food banks. Our results also apply to other problems involving the equitable and effective distribution of scarce resources under stochastic capacity and supply.
item.dc:creator: Irem Sengul Orgut, Julie S. Ivy, Reha Uzsoy, James Wilson

item.title: Convergence properties of nonlinear RLC electrical networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.01998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Convergence properties of general electrical networks with grounded nonlinear capacitors at the nodes and nonlinear inductors and resistors at the edges are studied. It is shown how, under appropriate conditions, for every initial condition there exists a unique equilibrium to which the system converges asymptotically. Partial extensions to networks with terminals or current sources are also provided. For RC networks this is compared with the use of an alternative storage function based on the co-content functions of the resistors.
item.dc:creator: Arjan van der Schaft

item.title: Minimax-Optimal Static Estimators Under Interference
item.description: arXiv:2611.02048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of estimating the global treatment effect in randomized experiments under interference, where a unit's outcome may depend on the treatment assignments of other units. We adopt a minimax framework, allowing an adversary to select an outcome function from a class of functions that satisfy bounded outcomes and bounded interference. We derive minimax-optimal static estimators that are robust to a wide range of interference structures, parameterized by a scalar $\delta$ controlling the maximum influence of one unit's treatment on another's outcome. Under large interference, we observe two regimes. When the treatment and control groups are equally sized, the minimax-optimal static estimator is the zero estimator. When one of the two groups is larger, the minimax-optimal static estimator is a "half-zero" estimator, in which the outcomes of the smaller group are ignored, and the estimator only considers the outcomes of the larger group.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Delarue, Ilan Lobel

item.title: Adaptive Preference Elicitation in Preference Robust CPT-Based Shortfall
item.description: arXiv:2611.02059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the cumulative prospect theory (CPT)-based shortfall risk measure where the value (utility) function and the distortion (probability weighting) functions are ambiguous. We propose a worst-case CPT-based shortfall risk measure where the capital requirement is based on the worst-case value function and distortion functions from an ambiguity set constructed with user-specific information (e.g., preference between risky and certain lotteries) and well-known general information such as the S-shape of the value functions. When the underlying random loss is discretely distributed and parameters in pairs of lotteries remain undetermined, we demonstrate that the worst-case value function and the distortion functions have a piecewise linear structure. Based on this observation, we develop an adaptive preference elicitation approach extended from the well-known polyhedral method to simultaneously elicit the distortion functions and the positive and negative parts of the value function by solving a sequence of mixed-integer linear programs. Based on the elicited distortions, we design new queries to construct a feasible set of the holistic value functions. The proposed framework iteratively shrinks the ambiguity set through designed queries, yielding a computationally implementable robust CPT-based shortfall risk measure. To examine the in-sample and out-of-sample performance of the elicited CPT-based preference functions and the resulting preference robust shortfall risk measure, we conduct numerical experiments under an S-shaped value function and inverse S-shaped distortion functions and report the corresponding results.
item.dc:creator: Sainan Zhang, Erick Delage, Huifu Xu

item.title: Split Cuts in Fixed Integer Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.02169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how many split cuts, which include the Gomory mixed-integer cuts, are needed to reach the integer hull, and how large split closures can be. In every fixed dimension, a rational pure-integer polytope admits a polynomial-time constructible split proof of its integer hull with polynomial total encoding length; consequently, its full split rank is polynomial in the input length. This establishes the split-rank conjecture of Basu, Conforti, Di Summa, and Jiang for bounded pure-integer polyhedra in fixed dimension. Central to our approach is a preservation result: in arbitrary pure-integer dimension, an inequality whose violating points map, under an integer-affine map, into the interior of a planar lattice-free polyhedron has a polynomial split proof retaining every point already satisfying it. Whereas Chv\'atal--Gomory closures have polynomial-size inequality descriptions in fixed dimension, split closures need not: tetrahedra of input length $\Theta(\log N)$ can have split closures with at least $2N-1$ facets, yet extension complexity $\Theta(\log N)$. For the two-row system $x=f+Rs$, $s\ge0$, $x\in\mathbb Z^2$ of input length $L$, the split closure has an exact extended formulation with $O(L)$ inequalities and auxiliary variables; this bound is tight. Separation over the split closure is polynomial-time in fixed total dimension. Finally, for mixed-integer feasible rational polytopes with fixed integer dimension $p$ and any continuous dimension, we maximize a primitive integral objective on the integer variables with $O_p(G+1)$ split cuts, each removing a current optimal LP vertex, until an optimal vertex is mixed-integer feasible; here $G$ is the integrality gap of the LP relaxation, rounded down.
item.dc:creator: Avinash Bhardwaj, Vishnu Narayanan

item.title: Integrating Data Center Flexibility into Power System Operations: A Framework for Temporal Redispatch
item.description: arXiv:2611.02228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rapid growth in data center electricity demand, driven by artificial intelligence (AI) training and inference, is expected to increase stress conditions for power grids. Operational flexibility from data centers offers a near-term lever to relieve such stresses. Existing models of data center flexibility tend to bundle economic incentives with physical constraints, obscuring the tradeoff between economic willingness to shift load and technical limitations to do so. This paper proposes a temporal-redispatch focused framework that decouples data center demand flexibility into two independently parameterized dimensions: (1) systematic flexibility, capturing the economic environment through penalties for temporal shifting of data centers' scheduled demand, and (2) operational flexibility, capturing the physical envelope through the demand shifting time window and the limit on shifted data center demand. The framework relies on a direct current optimal power flow (DC-OPF) linear program which enables annual parametric analysis at hourly resolution. The framework is studied using a synthetic grid mimicking the Texas transmission system populated with the 2026 Adjusted Forecast from ERCOT (Electric Reliability Council of Texas). Results show that operational flexibility imposes a physical lower bound on unsatisfied demand that no economic incentive can overcome; longer shifting windows and higher limits on shifted data center demand reduce operational cost with different impacts on grid utilization; and, temporal redispatch shaves system-wide net load peaks while partially compensating for localized transmission bottlenecks that emerge under modeled coal retirement scenarios.
item.dc:creator: Huansong Li, Erhan Kutanoglu, Michael Baldea, Ilias Mitrai

item.title: Small-time controllability of affine systems and quadratic Lie brackets
item.description: arXiv:2611.02293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a new sufficient condition for small-time global exact controllability of finite-dimensional control-affine systems. It points out that, under a natural Lie algebra rank condition, quadratic Lie brackets are the only possible obstacles to controllability. This result extends to infinite-dimensional settings such as the global approximate controllability of diffeomorphisms. It also allows us to interpret recent results in PDE control theory.
item.dc:creator: Karine Beauchard, Eugenio Pozzoli

item.title: Robust Closed-form Framework for Drag-Propulsive Control of Formation Flight
item.description: arXiv:2611.02321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To conserve propellant, Distributed Space Systems (DSS) can leverage environmental forces to produce low cost relative forces, such as atmospheric drag in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). This work maximizes this strategy by developing robust, closed-form algorithms for optimal "hybrid" control, defined here as complementing the magnitude and directionality deficiencies of differential drag with the superior control authority of propulsive maneuvers within the same control window. The use of drag introduces a significant source of dynamic uncertainty to the control problem, primarily from inaccurate atmospheric density modelling. This paper develops a robust control architecture that periodically re-solves the remaining drag maneuver plan in a diminishing horizon policy, rejecting operational and navigation errors while retaining the cost savings offered by differential drag. The approach is built upon reachable set theory, a control analysis technique that provides conditions for optimality for Linear Time Variant (LTV) systems with norm-like cost functions and optimally decouples hybrid control into separate propulsive and differential drag sub-problems. The optimality conditions are leveraged to prove the asymptotic Lyapunov stability of ideal reachable set-based control solutions and derive error bounds on this stability. A covariance analysis on the primary sources of error in hybrid control determines that the dominating source of uncertainty is the atmospheric density model. This conclusion allows the bounds on Lyapunov stability to be completely met by simply conditioning the atmospheric density value used in the control solutions. The derived Lyapunov stability bounds and performance of the algorithm are demonstrated experimentally in high fidelity full-force orbital simulations of the upcoming Space Weather Reconfigurable Multiscale Experiment (SWARM-EX) mission.

item.title: Fast Fuel-Optimal Constrained Impulsive Control with Application to Distributed Spacecraft
item.description: arXiv:2611.02322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work extends a reachable set theory approach for fuel-optimal control to incorporate convex and non-convex state, time, and magnitude constraints. The solver is designed from a new set of optimality conditions, derived by reformulating a single reachable set into multiple time-ordered, step-wise reachable set waypoint sub-problems, where a waypoint is the state reached after a given maneuver. Non-convex constraints are satisfied at each waypoint, preserving convexity at each sub-problem without needing to convexify the full control problem, enabling the computationally efficient identification of constrained optimal maneuvers, and guaranteeing a user-defined bound on constrained cost. To produce an optimal maneuver plan, the solver rolls out constrained trajectories until the remaining unconstrained solution adheres to the problem constraints. The fuel-optimal control problem considered by this work is broadly applicable to many fields and particularly significant to Distributed Space Systems (DSS). Multi-agent guidance and propulsive control techniques, often for small spacecraft at close separations, require guarantees of collision avoidance, efficient maneuvering to preserve a restricted fuel payload, and numerically-simple algorithms functional under on-board computational processing limitations. The proposed solver offers both user-defined bounds on constrained maneuver optimality and enhanced computational efficiency to directly address these challenges, and these capabilities are demonstrated comparatively against baseline solvers from the literature through Monte Carlo analysis on a variety of relevant DSS scenarios. Overall, this work enables the benefits of reachable set theory, namely computational efficiency and provable optimality, to be extended to control problems of higher fidelity.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proceedings of the 2025 IEEE Aerospace Conference, Big Sky, Montana, March 2025
item.dc:creator: Matthew Hunter, Simone D'Amico

item.title: Mean Field Games in Dynamic Ticket Pricing with Overselling and Cancellations
item.description: arXiv:2611.02402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend a finite-state Mean Field Game model of dynamic ticket pricing to allow overselling, stochastic cancellations, and terminal penalties for unresolved negative inventory. Cancellations generate upward inventory transitions, producing a bidirectional inventory process coupled with firms' pricing decisions. We formulate the representative-firm control problem and the population consistency conditions, and prove existence of a selected Markovian mean field equilibrium under the stated assumptions, including a compact price set and an explicit tie-breaking rule. Numerical experiments show that the quadratic terminal penalty can generate an endogenous soft-boundary mechanism that discourages progressively deeper overselling. Under a low-cancellation stress case, linear penalties more strongly reduce the prevalence of terminal overselling, whereas quadratic penalties reduce its conditional depth and lower-tail severity. A time-varying cancellation experiment suggests that anticipated future inventory recovery can support lower early prices and greater temporary overbooking exposure. Under the adopted demand normalization, stronger mean-field coupling is associated with lower equilibrium prices and slower inventory depletion. Together, these results provide a tractable framework for analyzing pricing and overbooking incentives in competitive ticket markets with cancellations.
item.dc:creator: Yuzhou Chen, Yumiharu Nakano
