item.title: Convex Reformulation of Minkowski-Sum Outer Approximation for Matrix Ellipsoids in Data-Driven Control
item.description: arXiv:2611.02553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Approximating Minkowski sums of matrix ellipsoids by a single matrix ellipsoid provides a tractable description of noise bounds for controller design from noisy data. Existing linear matrix inequality (LMI) conditions can be used to compute such approximations, but directly solving the resulting optimization problems can be computationally expensive. This paper develops an efficient method for finding a minimum-volume outer matrix ellipsoid under these LMI conditions. Although the corresponding problem for ordinary vector-valued ellipsoids is convex, the objective function in the matrix-valued case is nonconvex. We find that the problem admits an equivalent convex reformulation, which resolves this difficulty. We first eliminate the matrix variables using equivalent LMI transformations and objective monotonicity, leaving one positive scalar variable per matrix ellipsoid in the sum. We then show that the objective becomes convex after a logarithmic change of variables. The resulting problem contains neither LMI constraints nor matrix variables and can therefore be solved efficiently. Numerical experiments confirm that the proposed method is substantially faster than the LMI-based method. An application to data-driven control further illustrates the tradeoff between guaranteed control performance and computation time.
item.dc:creator: Taira Kaminaga, Hampei Sasahara

item.title: Optimal Annuitization, Consumption, and Investment with Costly Capital Injections
item.description: arXiv:2611.02558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a joint optimal decision of portfolio, consumption, and annuitization for a pension-plan manager who balances retirement consumption benefits against the cost of maintaining the solvency of pension account. The pension sponsor provides costly capital injection to prevent negative wealth. Annuity purchases are irreversible, and injected funds remain in the liquid account and earn interest. Using the Legendre transform, we derive a semi-explicit solution to the associated free-boundary problem and verify the optimality of the resulting strategies. We identify an endogenous annuity-income threshold separating injection-active and injection-inactive regions and characterize six policy regimes arising from the interplay between capital injections and consumption constraints. Compared with the no-injection benchmark, capital injections delay annuitization, alter the structure of the annuitization boundary, and permit positive holdings in risky assets even at zero liquid wealth. Numerical results further reveal that cheaper annuities may increase the expected capital contributions required from the pension sponsor.
item.dc:creator: Yijie Huang, Xiaoqing Liang, Jie Xiong, Xiang Yu

item.title: Supermodularity and robust optimization in elliptic PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2611.02573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study distributionally robust optimization problems constrained by semilinear elliptic PDEs. Uncertain nonnegative loads enter the PDE through $m$ intensity parameters, and damage is measured by integrating a nondecreasing convex function of the solution. We prove that, for coercive operators satisfying a positivity-preserving lattice condition, a nondecreasing concave reaction $g$ makes the damage nondecreasing, convex, and supermodular in the load intensities. Under nonnegative loading and $g(0)=0$, concavity is also necessary for these properties to hold for all admissible operators and damage functions. For Wasserstein uncertainty sets based on a weighted $\ell_1$ distance and $N$ observations, we show that at most $m+1$ nested stress corners are needed per observation. These corners form a set of at most $N(m+1)$ points that does not depend on the Wasserstein radius and supports a worst-case distribution for every radius. We compute the exact robust value by checking $\lambda=0$ and at most $Nm$ positive breakpoints, and we construct a worst-case distribution that moves each observation to a chain corner and splits at most one observation between two adjacent corners. We apply the results to a convex remediation-planning problem with Monod biodegradation. Numerical experiments show that the method requires far fewer PDE solves than enumerating all corners. Finally, a counterexample shows that supermodularity can fail for the fractional $p$-Laplacian when $p>2$.
item.dc:creator: Debangana Mukherjee, Akash Ashirbad Panda

item.title: Federated Affine Variational Inequalities: Exact Averaging and Complexity Limits
item.description: arXiv:2611.02598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the classical Local Stochastic Extragradient method (Local SEG) for monotone variational inequalities under intermittent communication, where devices perform several local oracle calls between synchronization rounds. For affine monotone mean operators, including nonsymmetric bilinear saddle systems, we prove that equal device averaging commutes pathwise with both stages of the stochastic extragradient update. Local trajectories may therefore drift apart while their mean follows a centralized stochastic-extragradient recursion driven by averaged noise. The identity remains valid when individual oracle realizations are nonlinear and query dependent. Under conditionally centered oracle errors that are conditionally independent across devices within each stage, the reduction yields a restricted weak-gap rate that uses the local sequential depth for deterministic progress and the aggregate oracle budget across devices for variance reduction. When every device makes at least two local oracle calls per communication round, the bound contains no additional mixed client-drift term and is also attained by a terminal-only aggregation schedule. An affine Gaussian lower bound matches the depth and sample dependences before statistical saturation for distributed zero-respecting algorithms; its statistical component applies to arbitrary randomized algorithms. A complementary lower bound for feasible distributed zero-respecting methods shows that bounded geometry and query-dependent noise can create an additional communication-locality obstruction. These results delineate the exact-averaging regime of unconstrained affine Local SEG and a complexity boundary that arises under active feasibility constraints.
item.dc:creator: Darina Dvinskikh, Kirill Novoselov, Alexander Gasnikov

item.title: Local null controllability of a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis system by a Neumann boundary control
item.description: arXiv:2611.02621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove local null controllability for a parabolic equation coupled to an elliptic equation on a bounded interval. The drift depends on the elliptic variable, and a single control acts through the Neumann condition at the left endpoint. For every positive control time and every locally Lipschitz drift function, sufficiently small initial data in $L^\infty$ can be driven to zero by an $L^\infty$ boundary control. To construct the control, we extend the linear equation to a larger interval using an even extension of the initial datum and an odd extension of the drift. A distributed $L^2$ control in the added interval then gives a boundary control on the original interval. A heat kernel estimate bounds the derivative trace needed for this construction. We obtain the nonlinear result by a set-valued fixed point argument.
item.dc:creator: Mohmedmunavvar Mubarak Bapu

item.title: Finite Recovery by Extrapolation for the Douglas--Rachford Method on Affine Subspaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.02694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We completely describe the dynamics of the Douglas--Rachford (DR) method for solving affine subspace feasibility. We characterise the affine hull of the resulting iterates, and we show how the corresponding search space's dimension is an explicit function of the number of distinct nontrivial principal angles. This dimension can be much smaller than the ambient dimension, helping to explain why extrapolation can be so effective. Using this characterisation, we extend the Lyapunov surrogate method (LSM) to higher extrapolation orders and prove that it recovers the DR limit exactly from finitely many iterates. We show that LSM and a least-squares extrapolation (LeSE) share the affine search spaces used by the generalized minimal residual method (GMRES) applied to the DR fixed-point equation (DR-GMRES). The dimension characterisation gives bounds on the number of steps required for exact recovery by all three methods. We develop adaptive implementations that estimate the search-space dimension from differences between successive DR iterates and use this estimate to select the extrapolation order. Numerical experiments show how ill-conditioning affects recovery accuracy, and we identify cases where adaptive extrapolation runs faster than DR-GMRES.
item.dc:creator: Jordan Collard, Scott B. Lindstrom

item.title: A counterexample to a three-step convergence bound for BFGS with exact line search
item.description: arXiv:2611.02719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We disprove a three-step error estimate for the Broyden--Fletcher--Goldfarb--Shanno {(BFGS)} method with exact line searches. We construct a globally strongly convex function $F\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ and a single nonterminating trajectory $x_k\to0$ for which $\limsup_{k\to\infty}\|x_{k+3}\|/(\|x_{k+2}\|\|x_k\|)=+\infty$. The Hessian of $F$ lies between $\tfrac12 I$ and $\tfrac32 I$ everywhere, and $F(x)-\tfrac12\|x\|^2$ is compactly supported with all derivatives vanishing at $0$. The proof first constructs point-gradient pairs satisfying the exact BFGS step identities. A five-step cycle produces a large three-step quotient and restores an invariant plane for the actual updated matrix, allowing the cycle to be repeated with arbitrarily small gradient errors. Disjoint smooth corrections to a quadratic then realize all the pairs by one objective. Strong convexity identifies the prescribed points with the unique exact line-search minimizers. Thus smoothness and strong convexity do not imply the proposed product estimate, even for an objective that agrees with a quadratic to every order at its minimizer.
item.dc:creator: Jiawei Xu, Jiang Hu

item.title: Inverse optimization for divisor methods of apportionment
item.description: arXiv:2611.02720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The apportionment problem is to allocate a fixed number of seats among regions in proportion to their populations. In this paper, we propose an inverse optimization approach to evaluate how fairly an observed apportionment treats each region. It is well known that every divisor method can be formulated as a separable discrete convex minimization problem. We introduce a weighted divisor method, in which a nonnegative weight is assigned to each region, as the forward problem. Then we formulate an inverse optimization problem that finds the weight vector closest to the all-one vector in the $\ell_1$-norm such that the observed apportionment is optimal for the forward problem. We show that the optimal weight vector is always unique and has a closed-form expression as the median of three values that depend on a single parameter. Based on this result, the inverse optimization problem is reduced to a one-dimensional monotone equation, and it can be solved in $O(n \log n)$ time, where $n$ is the number of regions. We also apply the proposed approach to the apportionment of the single-member districts of the House of Representatives of Japan.
item.dc:creator: Daiki Kawane, Hokuto Nagano, Yoichi Izunaga

item.title: Comparison Principle and Semi-Lagrangian Methods for a Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman System with Recursive Utility
item.description: arXiv:2611.02763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a system of coupled first-order Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equations arising in continuous-time heterogeneous agent models with recursive utility, a class of models that has attracted increasing attention in macroeconomics. The first part of the paper establishes a comparison principle for the system when preferences exhibit early resolution of uncertainty. A key ingredient in the proof is an ordinally equivalent transformation of the recursive utility representation. In the second part, we develop semi-Lagrangian schemes and iterative algorithms for solving the associated nonlinear discrete systems. For preferences exhibiting late resolution of uncertainty, we establish a first-order error estimate for the semi-Lagrangian approximation. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed methods yield results consistent with those obtained using the previously developed finite difference schemes.
item.dc:creator: Qing Tang

item.title: Equivalent Graphical Conditions for Angle Rigidity and Angle-Based Network Localization
item.description: arXiv:2611.02764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Angle rigidity theory provides a theoretical basis for characterizing the geometric shape of graphs embedded in the plane under angle constraints, and establishing global convergence of angle-based network localization algorithms. The related references, however, are largely restricted to graphs generated by triangulation or bilateration ordering, which are sufficient but not necessary for angle rigidity. This paper addresses this challenge by focusing on establishing the equivalence between angle constraints and bearing constraints. The conditions for cycle compatible frameworks (with possibly non-generic configurations) to be angle fixable are provided. Moreover, it is shown for the first time that Laman graphs equivalently characterize minimally globally angle rigid graphs, implying that a Laman graph is the simplest graph that allows a generic embedding in the plane to be uniquely determined by subtended angles. As an application, a distributed algorithm for angle-based sensor network localization is proposed, which guarantees global convergence under a much milder network topology condition than those in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Jinpeng Huang, Gangshan Jing, Kai Zhao, Yongduan Song

item.title: Graph splitting algorithms for inconsistent feasibility problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.02825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study graph splitting algorithms for feasibility problems involving closed and convex sets whose intersection may be empty. We characterize their minimal displacement vector, which is known to be the limit of the differences between successive iterates, in terms of a least-squares problem measuring disagreement between the sets according to the graph structure. We then specialize to closed affine subspaces, proving strong convergence of the shadow sequence to a solution of such a least-squares problem whenever one exists. Our analysis extends classical Douglas-Rachford results on best approximation pairs to graph splitting algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Rub\'en Campoy, C\'esar L\'opez-Pastor, David Torregrosa-Bel\'en

item.title: Frank-Wolfe is Approximate Broximal Gradient Descent
item.description: arXiv:2611.02942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the Frank-Wolfe method is an approximation of Broximal Gradient Descent (BroxGD), and hence of the ball-proximal method. For constrained minimization, the ball-proximal method minimizes the objective over the intersection of the feasible set with a ball around the current iterate. Linearizing the objective gives BroxGD, but the intersection can remain difficult to handle even when linear minimization over the feasible set alone is cheap. We therefore replace the intersection by a smaller copy of the feasible set, obtained by shrinking it toward the current iterate so that it lies inside the ball. Minimizing the linear model over this smaller set gives exactly Frank-Wolfe, with the shrinking factor as its step size. We examine what this approximation preserves and what it can lose. For smooth convex objectives on compact convex sets, Frank-Wolfe retains a linear-model decrease guarantee that gives it and BroxGD a common convergence proof, recovering the classical $O(1/k)$ bound. Among compact convex regions inside the ball chosen before the gradient is known, the smaller copy is the smallest that preserves the same linear-model decrease guarantee. Nevertheless, Frank-Wolfe can achieve much less linear-model decrease than BroxGD at the same radius. A simplex example illustrates the sparsity gained by restricting the region, while a family of triangles shows how Frank-Wolfe can lose the distance decrease guaranteed by BroxGD. We also give a computable test for recovering the distance guarantee and a refinement procedure that terminates after finitely many oracle calls on polytopes.
item.dc:creator: Peter Richt\'arik, Zhirayr Tovmasyan

item.title: Stability Filters for Receding-Horizon Games
item.description: arXiv:2611.02953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In receding-horizon games, self-interested players repeatedly solve a finite-horizon generalized Nash equilibrium problem (GNEP) and apply its first-stage actions. Ensuring stability of the resulting closed-loop system, however, is a challenging task that requires careful design of the players' strategies or additional constraints. We propose a stability filter that minimally modifies the variational equilibrium of the finite-horizon GNEP to enforce a prescribed decrease of a quadratic Lyapunov function. For receding-horizon games with linear dynamics, quadratic costs, and polyhedral coupling input constraints, whose associated GNEP is strongly monotone, we show that a filter always exists such that a closed-loop equilibrium exists, the filter is always feasible, does not intervene when the equilibrium already satisfies the decrease condition, and that renders the closed loop globally exponentially stable. Moreover, the filtered strategy is an $\epsilon$-generalized Nash equilibrium, with $epsilon$ vanishing exponentially along closed-loop trajectories.
item.dc:creator: Tatiana Tatarenko, Alberto Bemporad

item.title: Fischer-Burmeister-based Multiplier Dynamics in Inequality-Constrained Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.02991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study proportional-integral multiplier feedback for inequality-constrained optimization using the Fischer-Burmeister complementarity residual. We construct explicit dynamics and characterize gain-dependent stability and convergence rates. For a single active constraint, we derive exact local stability and decay-rate conditions, including a tradeoff between continuous-time convergence and discretization costs. For strongly convex objectives with affine constraints, we establish global convergence and characterize geometric conditions for uniform exponential stability. Numerical experiments compare feedback structures and computational costs.
item.dc:creator: Kang Liu, Jianchen Hu

item.title: Finite-horizon Optimal Consumption and Investment with Costly Income Adjustment
item.description: arXiv:2611.03076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study optimal consumption and investment for an investor who receives labor income until a fixed retirement date, can raise the income rate irreversibly at a constant price per unit of income flow, and cannot borrow against future income. A pathwise argument shows that no income is purchased during a final period before retirement whose length depends only on the interest rate and the price. Before this period the dual problem has two free boundaries: a lower one generated by the borrowing constraint and an upper one, at which income is purchased, that escapes to infinity as the final period begins. The analysis of this problem is our main mathematical contribution. During the final period it is a single obstacle problem, which we solve, together with the regularity of its free boundary, by established methods. Before that period a partial hodograph transformation straightens both free boundaries and turns the problem into a quasilinear parabolic equation with oblique boundary conditions on a fixed interval. Comparison principles, explicit barriers and regularity theory for quasilinear equations then give existence, uniqueness and smoothness. Transforming back and gluing the two constructions yields global regularity: both free boundaries are infinitely differentiable and the value function is a classical solution at every positive wealth level. A dual budget process verifies optimality. We also derive coupled Volterra integral equations for the free boundaries, prove exponential convergence to the perpetual problem under a scalar condition, and find numerically a purchase threshold that is U-shaped in the time to retirement.
item.dc:creator: Gugyum Ha, Junkee Jeon

item.title: Renting, Owning, and Moving: Housing Tenure Choice with Transaction Costs
item.description: arXiv:2611.03202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The wealth thresholds at which a household switches between renting and owning depend on its preferences, but the dates at which some owner sells or every renter buys do not. In our finite-horizon model, a household chooses consumption, a portfolio, and costly tenure changes while rents, ownership expenses, and transaction costs vary over time on announced dates. When financial markets span house-price risk, these dates are those of a deterministic minimum cost schedule for housing, discounted at the risk-adjusted housing carry and computed from a scalar reflected equation. Preferences, housing services, and labor income only locate the thresholds inside these timing windows, and house-price coefficients enter the dates only through the carry, because financial hedging offsets the exposure of the home. When owning costs at least as much as renting, the windows concern selling, and an anticipated selling surcharge closes the selling window before the surcharge peaks and keeps it closed for years afterwards. We also establish strong duality and the regularity of the thresholds and compute them by integral equations. Numerically, the windows disappear when short sales or borrowing are restricted but do not move with the preferences we vary under an uninsurable increase in the ownership cost.
item.dc:creator: Kexin Chen, Gugyum Ha, Junkee Jeon

item.title: Policy Iteration over Terminal Cost Functions: From LQR to MPC
item.description: arXiv:2611.03401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Policy iteration is a classical method for successively improving control policies in optimal control and reinforcement learning. In this paper, we propose a policy iteration framework that refines receding-horizon control (RHC) and model predictive control (MPC) policies online by iteratively updating the terminal cost. We first develop the framework for the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) problem. We show that the Riccati map is a contraction in the Thompson metric on an explicitly constructed invariant order interval. Using this property, we prove convergence of approximate policy iteration for finite-horizon RHC, where the terminal cost is given by an approximate value function. From an initial terminal cost, we then construct a robust invariant order interval within which the RHC policy is refined online. We extend the analysis to constrained MPC and present a constructive algorithm for safely updating the terminal ingredients, which guarantees recursive feasibility and asymptotic stability of the closed loop throughout the iterations. These results connect classical Riccati theory with approximate policy iteration and provide a principled pathway toward learning MPC terminal ingredients. A numerical example illustrates the proposed method.
item.dc:creator: Tren M. J. T. Baltussen (Maurice), Nathan P. Lawrence (Maurice), Alexander Katriniok (Maurice), Ali Mesbah (Maurice), W. P. M. H. (Maurice), Heemels

item.title: Newtonian Dynamics in Metric Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.03443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a variational framework for second-order, frictionless (Newtonian) dynamics in metric spaces, extending the metric theory of curves of maximal slope from gradient flows to evolutions with inertia. The construction rests on three pillars, mirroring the first-order theory. First, we introduce a class of second-order absolutely continuous curves, characterized by a geometric--variational inequality on families of tangent geodesics, and define a metric notion of acceleration. Second, we define curves of Newtonian motion as the curves achieving equality in an energy inequality involving an upper gradient--Hessian pair, which in Hilbert spaces is equivalent to Newton's equation $\ddot\gamma = -\nabla E(\gamma)$. Third, we propose a two-step predictor--corrector minimizing movement scheme and show that its discrete interpolants satisfy approximate versions of these inequalities. Under extendability and interceptor conditions on geodesics---which are satisfied, for instance, by geodesically uniformly complete, locally compact spaces with curvature bounded below---and under suitable regularity assumptions on the energy, we prove that the scheme converges, up to subsequences, to a curve of Newtonian motion. As an illustration, we recover the linear wave equation as a curve of Newtonian motion driven by the Dirichlet energy. This paper is complemented by the companion paper [Fornasier, Klemenc, Scagliotti, "A Lions Lift Framework for Gradient and Newtonian Evolutions in Wasserstein spaces"], which specifies and adapts the results to the Wasserstein metric space $(\mathcal{P}_2,W_2)$ through Lions lift, which explains Vlasov equations as Newtonian flows on spaces of probability measures.
item.dc:creator: Massimo Fornasier, Jona Klemenc, Alessandro Scagliotti

item.title: Wasserstein accelerated proximal gradient algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2611.03524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose accelerated proximal gradient methods for composite optimization problems on the quadratic Wasserstein space of probability measures, including Kullback--Leibler divergence minimization. The objective function consists of a smooth geodesically convex functional and a possibly nonsmooth regularizer that is convex along generalized geodesics. The convexity and smoothness conditions on the smooth component are imposed only on the feasible set. As a preliminary result, we establish the equivalence between geodesic convexity of the smooth functional on the feasible set and convexity of its Hilbert-space lift on the corresponding feasible set. Assuming exact proximal steps, we prove an $O(k^{-2})$ convergence rate for the objective gap when the smooth component is geodesically convex and accelerated linear convergence when it is geodesically strongly convex. We also describe particle approximations of these algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Kansei Ushiyama, Yi Feng, Kaito Fujii, Yuma Fujimoto, Noboru Isobe

item.title: ParaDeAl: Parallel Descent Algorithms for Sparse Statistics
item.description: arXiv:2611.03529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Best subset selection is a central problem in statistical regression, drawing increasing attention from the broader optimization and machine learning communities. Solving the hard L0 sparsity constraint directly has been computationally challenging; as a result, most existing work proposes formulations which do not enforce the constraint, but instead use a mix of L0/L1/L2 penalties to encourage sparsity. Modern methods for solving such penalized formulations are tractable for p = 100,000, but give up direct control over sparsity. In this paper, we propose a two-stage proximal gradient descent-based approach which both enforces the sparsity constraint and incorporates L1/L2 penalties, leveraging GPUs for computational acceleration to find approximate solutions. Our method, ParaDeAl, offers the user the ability to select the problem hyperparameters, solves all configurations in parallel, and obtains solutions up to 15x faster than the best state-of-the-art CPU competitors while achieving almost identical test accuracy for the same support size for large (p > 100,000) synthetic and real-world datasets.
item.dc:creator: Adam Deng, Rahul Mazumder

item.title: Dynamical Unbalanced Optimal Transport: Duality, Reachability, and Computation
item.description: arXiv:2611.03573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study dynamical unbalanced optimal transport for nonlinear control-affine systems in which the control input affects both the transportation of mass and its growth or decay. This phenomenon arises naturally in controlled transport-reaction systems such as cancer treatment, and distinguishes the problem from standard unbalanced optimal transport, where transport and mass variation are typically independent. To address this problem, we combine classical relaxed-control theory with a weighted superposition principle to obtain an infinite-dimensional linear programming reformulation over weighted trajectories. Under suitable convexity and compactness assumptions, we show that this relaxation is tight. Based on the relaxation, we derive a Kantorovich dual formulation in terms of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman inequalities, and establish strong duality over smooth subsolutions. We then utilize the dual formulation to characterize reachability of the system, namely, when a given terminal measure is reachable from a given initial measure. In addition, tractable sufficient conditions for reachability are provided. Finally, we develop an augmented-Lagrangian algorithm based on the dual formulation for numerical computation of the optimal transport plan. The framework is illustrated on a phenotype-structured cancer treatment problem in which therapy simultaneously drives phenotypic adaptation and population growth or death.
item.dc:creator: Dongjun Wu, Anders Rantzer

item.title: PDFP: GPU-Accelerated Feasibility Pump via PDHG
item.description: arXiv:2611.03629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The feasibility pump (FP) is among the most widely used primal heuristics for mixed-integer linear programming. It alternates between rounding an LP-feasible point and projecting the rounded point back onto the feasible region of the LP relaxation. Recent pump-based heuristics compute the projection with the primal--dual hybrid gradient method (PDHG), which is scalable on modern GPUs. They pose it as a linear program, which needs auxiliary variables and constraints for general integers. Once the projection runs on the GPU, the constraint-propagation rounding (CPR) of FP~2.0 takes a large share of each iteration. For the projection, we propose PDFP, a custom first-order method that solves the pump's projection problem directly, without auxiliary primal variables or constraints. We prove that it keeps the accelerated linear rate of restarted Halpern PDHG. For the rounding, we propose a new procedure that is more efficient than CPR and, under certain assumptions, still returns a CPR rounding. It also chooses rounded values by constraint violation, which can produce feasible roundings where nearest rounding cannot. Finally, our pump runs two independent trajectories concurrently on one GPU through CPU--GPU synchronization. This exploits the variance in trajectory length and lets the pump terminate sooner on average. Computational experiments on MIPLIB~2017 instances show early, promising results: these contributions speed up the discovery of the first incumbent solution. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/MIT-Lu-Lab/PDFP.
item.dc:creator: Ruofeng Liu, Haihao Lu, Rahul Mazumder

item.title: A Triangular Log-Det PDHG for Semidefinite Programming: Complementarity Selection and Global Linear Convergence
item.description: arXiv:2611.03638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semidefinite programming (SDP) is an important class of convex optimization problems with wide applications in practice. In this paper, we study a solution-selection question for first-order methods for solving SDPs: Can a first-order method provably select a strictly complementary solution when one exists, and a maximally complementary solution otherwise? We propose Triangular Log-Det PDHG (TriLog-PDHG), a primal-dual hybrid gradient method equipped with a triangular log-determinant Bregman kernel. We show that TriLog-PDHG converges to a KKT point for any fixed positive shift and to a maximally complementary solution for every sufficiently small positive shift. When a strictly complementary solution exists, the unshifted method provably selects a strictly complementary KKT point and enjoys a global linear convergence rate. Under the same condition, we further develop an averaged and adaptively restarted variant that accelerates convergence. Numerical experiments on classical examples and SDPLIB instances illustrate the complementarity-selection and convergence properties predicted by the theory.
item.dc:creator: Lijun Ding, Jinwen Yang

item.title: A New Formulation of the Elastica Model with Application to Image Inpainting
item.description: arXiv:2611.00110v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Curves and interfaces play a central role in computer vision and image processing, and Euler's elastica energy is one of the most successful tools to model and manipulate them. The elastica energy is usually computed through a level-set or a phase field representation of the curve, in which the curvature term makes the energy nonlinear, non-convex and, in the level-set case, non-differentiable, so that its minimization is notoriously difficult. In this paper, we propose a new formulation of the elastica model based on a binary representation of curves. The key ingredient is a very simple formula for the curvature: if $\phi$ is the $\pm1$ binary function associated with a curve $\Gamma$, then along $\Gamma$ the curvature is given by $-\frac{1}{C_0\epsilon}\left(R_\epsilon *\phi\right)+O(\epsilon)$, where $R_\epsilon$ is a radial kernel supported in a ball of radius $\epsilon$ and $C_0$ is an explicit constant. No derivative of $\phi$ is involved and the convolution is evaluated by FFT. The resulting energy is a weighted total variation, so that formally the new formulation is a generalization of the well-known ROF model; a phase field type model is obtained from the same curvature formula. Combining FFT with the split Bregman iteration, which for the present problem coincides with an augmented Lagrangian method (ALM), we obtain efficient algorithms whose subproblems are either linear systems solved by conjugate gradient or explicit pointwise formulas. Numerical experiments on the inpainting of binary images are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Zuoqiang Shi, Xue-Cheng Tai

item.title: The Prior-Force Family of Implicit Denoiser Priors and Its Decisions in Linear Inverse Problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.00183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Implicit priors given by Gaussian denoisers successfully regularize a wide range of inverse problems in approaches such as plug-and-play (PnP), regularization by denoising (RED) and score-based methods. Such a prior depends on the noise level, and how it selects among signals consistent with the data remains largely uncharacterized. To put implicit and explicit priors on the same footing, we define the prior-force family $W_t=t^{-1}(D_t^{-1}-I)$ of any Gaussian denoiser $D_t$ at noise variance $t>0$ (inverse in the graph sense), the normalized denoising residual as an operator on clean signals. At a common effective prior weight, the equilibrium equations differ only in their prior terms: PnP uses $W_t$, RED/score-based methods the score force (the normalized residual as an operator on noisy inputs), and maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation the MAP force (the negative log-prior gradient). For the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) denoisers of a prior $\pi$, we compare the corresponding energies at three levels. Without observation, raising the noise level favors PnP minima that retain more posterior variance. On signals consistent with the data, the leading-order PnP energy for separated modes is the proximal hull of the MAP energy, which lets PnP select signals between modes; modes of equal data fit are ranked by peak height at small noise levels and by mass at large ones. For recovery, $W_t$ at the truth bounds the local bias, and an oracle noise level balances this bias against denoiser error. These results show that the noise level is a parameter of the prior rather than a step size. Experiments with exact priors support these predictions, including the mixture components that PnP selects on unseen data.
item.dc:creator: Weijie Liang, Chuling Wen, Jian Lu

item.title: ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning
item.description: arXiv:2611.00236v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) enables parameter-efficient fine-tuning but can suffer from redundant basis directions. Constraining the basis factor to the Stiefel manifold addresses this redundancy through orthonormality. Landing methods allow temporarily infeasible iterates to explore a neighborhood of the manifold while progressively restoring orthogonality without per-step retractions. To improve optimization efficiency while retaining this flexibility, we introduce ProLand (Product-space Landing), a retraction-free optimizer that combines coordinated factor updates with Muon-style spectral directions. By designing the updates in the space of the represented weight increment, ProLand separates objective optimization from orthogonality restoration, supporting efficient feasibility recovery. This coordinated construction also enables Muon-style directions to guide objective optimization while preserving that separation. Experiments cover four GLUE validation tasks on DeBERTa-v3-base and seven language benchmarks on Qwen2.5-3B, Llama-3.2-3B, and Moonlight-16B-A3B across multiple adapter ranks. Across these 11 tasks, ProLand achieves the highest average score among the compared methods in every tested encoder and decoder model-rank configuration.
item.dc:creator: Chenyu Zhou, Yuxuan Zeng, Qi Deng, Dongdong Ge, Yinyu Ye

item.title: Measurement-angle control of a continuously monitored quantum oscillator: purification limits and optimal protocols
item.description: arXiv:2611.00410v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the dynamic purification of a continuously monitored quantum harmonic oscillator coupled to a thermal bath, where the control is the quadrature measurement angle of up to two detectors with prescribed strengths and efficiencies. Within the Gaussian regime, the conditional state covariance obeys a deterministic Riccati equation, and we ask what purity can be reached and sustained by manipulating the angle in time, in analogy with rapid-purification protocols for qubits. We propose, analyze, and compare constant-rate, greedy, vibrational, and variational monitoring strategies on the basis of sustained purity starting from the thermal bath state, and quantify to what extent they are able to maintain higher purity levels compared to lab-fixed or phase-locked detectors. We highlight structural features, operational limits, and optimal protocols from each strategy and study how model parameters shape control performance. We observe that in the absence of measurement-frame anisotropy, the time-dependent strategies achieve higher but similar performance. Once this symmetry is broken, their performances diverge, either improving or worsening depending on the relative timescales of oscillator dynamics, thermalization, and measurement.
item.dc:creator: Ralph Sabbagh, Olga Movilla Miangolarra, Andrew N. Jordan, Tryphon T. Georgiou

item.title: Some Remarks on the Asymptotic Behavior of Mean Field Games of Controls
item.description: arXiv:2611.00490v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze the asymptotic behavior of several mean field games of controls. First, in the time-dependent case, we examine the behavior of solutions to discounted mean field games of controls as the discount factor $\lambda$ tends to infinity. Next, we study three stationary models of mean field games of controls, finding that solutions to the first-order discounted problem and the second-order ergodic problem can be obtained from solutions to the second-order discounted problem by taking $\nu \to 0$ and $\lambda \to 0$, respectively. Finally, we investigate the long-time average behavior of solutions to the time-dependent system with no discount, finding that solutions converge to the solution to the second-order ergodic problem as $T \to \infty$.
item.dc:creator: Jameson Graber, Elizabeth Matter, Kyle Rosengartner

item.title: Non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD with discontinuous stochastic gradients: a new route to portfolio CVaR minimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.00578v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conditional-Value-at-Risk (CVaR) optimization is a fundamental tool in portfolio selection, yet its nonsmooth loss structure poses a challenge for the existing theory of stochastic gradient methods including associated Langevin algorithms. In particular, the positive-part loss and the softmax portfolio parametrization lead to stochastic gradients that need not be globally Lipschitz continuous, but rather discontinuous, where available non-convex stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) guarantees often exhibit an unfavorable exponential dependence on the problem dimension. In this article, we develop a non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD for a regularized CVaR portfolio optimization problem. We exploit the geometric structure of the CVaR objective to establish linear growth, convexity-at-infinity, and one-sided Lipschitz properties of the stochastic gradient without imposing density assumptions on the asset losses that are typical in previous works. Crucially, the constants appearing in the aforementioned structural conditions are shown to be independent of the number of assets. Moreover, we establish a convergence bound in Wasserstein-2 distance with rate $\mathcal{O}(\lambda^{1/4})$ and a finite-time guarantee for the expected excess risk. Our analysis, together with the dimension-independent constants in the structural conditions, leads to an excess risk bound that depends linearly on the number of assets. Numerical experiments with simulated Gaussian portfolios exhibit the predicted dimension dependence. Computational comparisons with alternative stochastic optimization methods further illustrate the practical efficiency of SGLD for the optimization problem under consideration. Finally, we extend the framework to a broader class of non-convex stochastic optimization problems with discontinuous stochastic gradients.
item.dc:creator: Yan Ding, Sotirios Sabanis, Ying Zhang

item.title: Conic Certification of Transformer Attention
item.description: arXiv:2611.00585v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Attention is the computational core of large language models, yet the verifiers that bound how far an attention head's output can move under input perturbations give no guarantee on how loose their bounds are. A weak certificate therefore cannot be told apart from a fragile model. We develop a conic programming theory of attention certification that supplies this guarantee. We prove that the difficulty lies not in the softmax but in the bilinear interaction of a varying query with the keys. This interaction makes certification NP-hard over boxes and inapproximable once the attention logits can move by a constant amount. A fixed query or listed token substitutions, by contrast, make the exact worst case efficiently computable. An exponential cone moment relaxation then certifies a head with an error bounded quadratically in the perturbation radius by computable quantities, an order that cannot be improved. We also show that relaxations that treat a network one operation at a time, linear bound propagation among them, pay on second-order terms a sum of per-operation maxima instead of one coupled maximum. Computational results on GPT-2 indicate that the theory carries over to a trained model. Against exact worst cases with the query fixed, the certificate attains the predicted second-order accuracy. It is tighter than linear bound propagation on every head, and the looseness of bound propagation tracks the predicted per-operation excess.
item.dc:creator: Masoud Ataei

item.title: Unbiased Low-Rank Approximation for Repeated Matrix-Vector Multiplication: Stability and Optimal Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2611.00787v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Replacing the matrix in an iteration with random low-rank matrices can reduce the cost of matrix-vector multiplication. However, even if the sampled matrices equal the original matrix in expectation, the expected squared norm of the random iterates may grow while the original iteration converges. Under a fixed rank bound, we study how to choose the distribution of these random matrices to minimize this growth when sampling independently at each step. We derive an exact formula for the optimal asymptotic growth factor and use it to determine when the expected squared norm can converge to zero. We then characterize precisely when a fixed sampling distribution achieves this optimal factor and construct finite-support optimal distributions in every attainable case. These results determine the minimum rank required for stability and provide optimal sampling designs under the prescribed rank constraint.
item.dc:creator: Kang Liu

item.title: Entropy-Regularized Reinforcement Learning for the Regime-Switching Consumption-Investment Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.01046v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper establishes an entropy-regularized reinforcement learning (ERRL) framework for the continuous-time consumption-investment problem under a regime-switching market model with general utility functions. By incorporating randomized exploratory policies and Shannon entropy regularization into the stochastic optimal control formulation, we derive closed-form representations for the optimal exploratory consumption and investment strategies. Specifically, the optimal investment strategy follows a multivariate Gaussian distribution, whereas the optimal consumption strategy takes the form of a Gibbs measure---which specializes to a Gamma distribution under logarithmic utility and a non-standard exponential distribution under power utility. Crucially, our theoretical analysis reveals that the classical deterministic optimal decisions correspond to the mode---rather than the mean---of these exploratory distributions. Furthermore, we establish the convergence of the exploratory value function to its classical unregularized counterpart as the temperature parameter vanishes. For algorithmic design, we develop a continuous-time q-learning framework grounded in a novel continuous-time q-function, prove the policy improvement theorem, and establish martingale characterizations for both on-policy and off-policy learning. We find that parameterizing the actor network based on theoretical distribution families can help accelerate convergence and enhance numerical stability. Furthermore, numerical experiments across regime-switching environments provide empirical support for our theoretical findings, demonstrating stable loss convergence as well as the monotonicity and concavity of the learned value functions.
item.dc:creator: Congde Hu, Danping Li, Xun Li, Yijie Zeng

item.title: Lower Bounds on Inference Complexity for Polyak-Ruppert Averaged Stochastic Gradient Descent
item.description: arXiv:2611.01155v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish sharp lower bounds for Gaussian approximation of Polyak-Ruppert averaged stochastic gradient descent with polynomially decreasing step sizes. For every fixed exponent $\gamma\in(1/2,1)$, a single one-dimensional smooth, strongly convex example has approximation error with the limiting variance of order $n^{1/2-\gamma}+n^{\gamma-1}$ in Kolmogorov and convex distances. This matches the existing upper bound throughout the range of $\gamma$. The nonlinear bias contributes $n^{1/2-\gamma}$ even when the Gaussian reference uses the finite linearized variance. We also derive a lower bound of order $n^{-(1-\gamma)/2}$ for the relative mean error of estimating the limiting variance from one SGD trajectory, uniformly over a scalar quadratic family. With the limiting variance known, achieving approximation error $\varepsilon$ on this example takes order $\varepsilon^{-4}$ iterations for the best choice $\gamma=3/4$. Achieving both Gaussian approximation and relative mean variance-estimation errors at most $\varepsilon$ uniformly over the model class requires at least order $\varepsilon^{-6}$ iterations for every fixed $\gamma$.
item.dc:creator: Denis Belomestny, Alexey Naumov, Sergey Samsonov

item.title: Adaptive Optimizers Can Get a Policy Ranking Wrong: Momentum, Dependent Data, and a Two-Run Remedy
item.description: arXiv:2611.01216v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Operators choosing among decision rules, such as when a battery charges or where an idle taxi goes, rank them by estimated long-run value. A standard estimator, linear temporal-difference (TD) learning, fits values from one stream of correlated observations. Large fits often use an adaptive optimizer, such as adaptive moment estimation (Adam), with fixed averaging rates. We show that these rates can change what is estimated, not just how fast: the same observations drive the updates and the optimizer's step-size scaling, moving the fit away from the intended TD value. The shift differs across rules, so it need not cancel in a comparison, and more data only makes a wrong ranking look more certain. Our remedy refits the same data at a second averaging rate that halves the effective gain, the number to which the leading shift is proportional. Twice the new fit minus the original removes that shift. In New York taxi and battery models calibrated to real data, common optimizer settings leave the selected rule unchanged but order close rules wrongly and misstate its value. Our remedy corrects nearly every wrong ordering, with one extra fit when the shift is moderate and two when it is larger.
item.dc:creator: Sunyoung An, Xiaoming Huo

item.title: How Much Can Approximate Equilibria Change the Social Cost of Selfish Routing?
item.description: arXiv:2611.01234v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study approximate Nash equilibria in nonatomic congestion games, with the goal of understanding how much the social cost can change when the equilibrium condition is relaxed. We consider $\epsilon$-approximate Nash equilibria ($\epsilon$-NE), in which each player uses a strategy whose cost is at most $1 + \epsilon$ times the minimum available cost. We compare the social costs of $\epsilon$-NE and exact Nash equilibria. This lets us quantify, for example, how much a navigation app can reduce total travel time when drivers tolerate routes slightly slower than the fastest available route. For degree-$d$ polynomial latencies in both general nonatomic congestion games and single-commodity routing games on series-parallel networks, we give tight lower and upper bounds on the relative change in social cost from an exact Nash equilibrium to any $\epsilon$-NE, with matching instances for every $\epsilon$. For small $\epsilon$, the largest possible relative reduction and increase in general congestion games are both $\Theta(\sqrt{d\epsilon})$, independently of the number of resources and populations. In contrast, on series-parallel networks of depth $h$, the largest possible relative reduction is $\Theta(h\epsilon)$, while the largest possible relative increase is known to be $\epsilon$. For the classes of games we study, these results give a tight and quantitative characterization of the possible changes in social cost and establish a separation between general and series-parallel networks.
item.dc:creator: Yu Cheng, Tianle Jiang

item.title: Dual Path Following for an Aerial Manipulator Under State and Input Constraints via Transverse Feedback Linearization
item.description: arXiv:2611.01442v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies dual path following for a quadrotor carrying a three-degree-of-freedom arm. The center of mass of the combined system must follow a vehicle path and the end effector must follow a second path, while the arm respects its joint limits and avoids its singular postures. The vehicle and the arm are mechanically coupled, so one controller must handle both paths. With the center of mass and the end-effector path coordinates as outputs, and a dynamic extension of the thrust, the system admits a normal form without internal dynamics. We characterize the states where this normal form fails. We formulate the transverse feedback linearizing controller as a quadratic program that relaxes only the speed of the end effector along its path and imposes safety and actuator limits as inequality constraints. The program reduces to a scalar problem with a closed-form solution. If it remains strictly feasible for all time, the feedback is locally Lipschitz, both paths are invariant and attractive, and every constraint holds. In the physics engine Drake, the controller resolves a conflict between the two speed references by slowing the end effector while both paths remain invariant. By contrast, a cascade with a safety filter leaves both paths. Code and animations are available at https://gradslab.github.io/am_dual_pf-/
item.dc:creator: Hamza Tariq, Adeel Akhtar

item.title: Long-time behavior of first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations in the Wasserstein space
item.description: arXiv:2611.01479v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the long-time behavior of solutions $U$ to first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations in the Wasserstein space $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb T^d)$. For a class of Hamiltonians with quadratic growth, including non-convex ones, we prove that there exist a unique ergodic constant $\lambda$ and a solution $V$ of the associated ergodic problem such that $U(t,m)-\lambda t$ converges to $V(m)$, uniformly on $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb T^d)$, as $t\to+\infty$. Finally, we provide applications to mean field control problems and zero-sum differential games.
item.dc:creator: Erhan Bayraktar, Antonios Zitridis

item.title: Learning Gradients of Homogeneous Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01530v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Homogeneous gradient functions have widespread significance, including applications in maximum energy subspace selection and retrieval problems. Euler's homogeneous function theorem specifies how the potential associated with a positively k-homogeneous gradient field can be recovered directly from the field itself. We use Euler's theorem to build on GradNets and propose a homogeneous gradient network architecture that is guaranteed to correspond to the gradient of a homogeneous function. Then, we describe how monotone homogeneous GradNets universally approximate the gradients of k-homogeneous convex functions. The inductive bias of homogeneous GradNets enables them to outperform baseline ICNNs by up to 7dB in our max energy subspace projection experiment and by up to 13% higher accuracy, 98% fewer parameters, and 70% fewer FLOPS in our amortized inner product search experiment.
item.dc:creator: Mayur S. Gowda, Srinivasa Pranav, Shreyas Chaudhari, Jos\'e M. F. Moura

item.title: Mean Field Game Problem with Kantorovich Potential Coupling: An Attrition model
item.description: arXiv:2611.01616v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work we address a class of Mean-Field Game (MFG) systems on the flat torus $\mathbb{T}^{d}$ in which individual agent incentives arise from macroscopic, distribution-dependent objectives governed by the Wasserstein-2 ($W_{2}$) distance. Taking the first variation (Lions derivative) of the Wasserstein-based macroscopic functional yields a coupled forward-backward system of Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) and Fokker--Planck (FP) equations featuring a nonlocal coupling driven by the Kantorovich optimal transport potential. As a primary case study, we formulate a large-scale attacker-defender attrition model aimed at protecting High-Value Units (HVUs). By defining population-wise attrition rates via the $W_{2}$ metric and casting the defense strategy as a Pareto-optimal McKean--Vlasov control problem, we derive a concrete HJB--FP system with a Kantorovich potential coupling. We prove the local-in-time existence of classical solutions for this system using Schauder's fixed-point theorem. Finally, we compute the MFG dynamics by combining the Sinkhorn algorithm with ResNet-based Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), and simulate two-dimensional attacker-defender engagements across diverse attrition parameters, control costs, and multi-HVU configurations.
item.dc:creator: Avetik Arakelyan, Davit Alaverdyan, Naira Hovakimyan, Isaac Kaminer, Tigran Bakaryan

item.title: Convex Regression at Scale: Geometry-Preserving Constraint Sparsification
item.description: arXiv:2611.01744v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Convex regression provides a flexible nonparametric estimation framework while incorporating appropriate shape information. However, its standard least-squares formulation has $O(n^2)$ supporting-hyperplane constraints creating a computational bottleneck as the sample size $n$ increases. We study a $K$-nearest-neighbor (KNN) localized relaxation for convex regression where we for each sample, we only maintain the $K$ nearest hyperplane constraints. Under mild regularity conditions, we establish statistical guarantees for our modified estimator in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. In particular, for $d>4$, the population risk of our modified problem can be shown to have equivalent convergence rates as the original least square convex regression estimator of $\widetilde O(n^{-2/d})$ using neighborhoods sizes (i.e. $K=K_n$) of order $\widetilde O(n^{2(d-1)/(2d-1)})$ for general convex functions and $\widetilde O(n^{(d+1)/(d+2)})$ for strongly convex functions. To corroborate our theory, we implement iterative optimization methods to compare the prediction accuracy of the KNN relaxation with those of the full estimator across synthetic convex benchmarks. Our experiments demonstrate that KNN prediction risk approaches the full-estimator prediction risk at neighborhood sizes matching the theoretical scale.
item.dc:creator: Anish Senapati, Jose Blanchet

item.title: IncVNM: An Interactive Recommender System with Incremental von Neumann-Morgenstern Utility Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.01786v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In modern recommender systems, users are often presented with products whose outcomes are random. The values of such products depend on their entire outcome distributions and on users' attitudes toward risk, making them difficult to evaluate using traditional product-level recommendation methods. We propose \textsc{IncVNM}, an interactive recommender system that incrementally learns a user-specific von Neumann--Morgenstern (VNM) utility function from ordinal click feedback generated during ordinary webpage browsing. At each interaction, \textsc{IncVNM} converts the click order within a displayed product list into pairwise comparisons between outcome distributions and updates the nominal utility by minimizing its deviation from the previous estimate while incorporating the newly observed pairwise comparisons. To close the interaction loop, an entropy-regularized sampling policy balances exploitation of the learned utility against exploration for additional preference information. We evaluate \textsc{IncVNM} in a rolling-window experiment with different response-error probabilities and show that it substantially outperforms the expected-return, mean--variance, discounted-UCB, and distribution-aware BPR baselines.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxin Wei, Jia Liu

item.title: OC-OPD: Observation-coordinated Supervision for On-Policy Distillation
item.description: arXiv:2611.01965v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reverse and forward Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergences provide complementary supervision in on-policy distillation: reverse KL refines the student's active token rankings, and forward KL allocates mass to teacher-supported candidates. At student-generated prefixes, we form a four-observation matrix by treating the student and teacher as both candidate sources and evaluators. The diagonal self-observations measure uncertainty, while source-centered cross-observations recover the two KL objectives. We establish an exact identity equating the Fisher inverse-metric coupling of their logit gradients with the sum of these contrasts, yielding a common local descent direction for distinct positive distributions. Observation-coordinated on-policy distillation (OC-OPD) uses observations to set preferences, closed-form bargaining to coordinate gradients, and distributional discrepancy to scale the update. Across three heterogeneous student settings (non-thinking generation, thinking generation, and base-model initialization), OC-OPD achieves strong gains in mathematical reasoning and transfers effectively to out-of-distribution scientific question answering and code generation. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/RuoranXu/OC-OPD.
item.dc:creator: Ruoran Xu, Yilun Zhao, Ziyu Chen, Arman Cohan

item.title: Rare Event Constrained Reinforcement Learning with Large Deviations
item.description: arXiv:2611.02055v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study finite-horizon reinforcement learning with a safety constraint on the probability of reaching a failure set. In contrast to the well-studied safe reinforcement learning literature, we consider problems where the probability of reaching the failure set is vanishingly small, but the consequences of reaching the failure set are catastrophic. Direct simulation and estimation of the optimal policy is naturally ineffective when the failure probability is extremely small. Moreover, on a real system the controller can only choose actions, and this is not enough to make failures frequent. In contrast to the rare event simulation literature, our goal is not to estimate the probability of the rare event occurrence, but to upper bound it such that the failure constraint is satisfied. Thus, instead of sampling failures, we use the large deviations principle. We define a damage variable that on exceeding a certain threshold indicates failure. We study the cumulant generating function (CGF) as its positive root provides an upper bound on the failure probability via Cramer's theorem. We extend this approach to Markov decision processes with hitting times through state-action CGFs, and give finite-horizon and state-dependent versions of the bound. The state-action CGFs do not depend on the policy and can be estimated from regular transitions, so the bound can be checked for any policy a priori. This gives a policy improvement algorithm in which every policy satisfies the failure constraint with high probability.
item.dc:creator: Rahul Misra

item.title: The local-to-global minimum problem of Calvert and Vamanamurthy: a quartic counterexample in three variables and the cubic case in all dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.02068v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In 1980 Calvert and Vamanamurthy asked whether a polynomial whose only critical point is a local minimum must attain its global minimum there. They gave counterexamples of every degree at least five in two or more variables and settled cubics in two and three variables and quartics in two variables, leaving open quartics in three or more variables and cubics in four or more variables. We resolve both remaining cases. First, we give an explicit quartic in three variables whose unique critical point is a nondegenerate strict local minimum, although the polynomial is unbounded below; the example extends to every dimension at least three, and its critical locus is a single point even over the complex numbers. Second, we prove that in every dimension a polynomial of exact degree three with a local minimum has another critical point, so that the cubic case holds vacuously; the proof is elementary and avoids the topological degree arguments used previously in two and three variables. Together with the results of Calvert and Vamanamurthy, this gives the complete classification of the local-to-global property by degree and dimension.
item.dc:creator: Hugo Adu\'en

item.title: Overcoming Demand Censoring through Randomization for Risk-Sensitive Newsvendor Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.02267v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study online newsvendor learning with bounded demand, censored observations, and convex nonlinear shortage costs. Because stockouts can conceal the shortage magnitudes needed by gradient-based algorithms, we use randomized ordering to construct unbiased subgradient estimates. We characterize admissible randomization distributions within this framework and develop an online inventory policy that combines the resulting subgradient estimates with gradient-based updates. Our regret analysis quantifies the cost of randomization via the estimation variance and an additional loss term. We characterize the randomization distributions that minimize this objective. For piecewise-linear shortage costs, the optimal distribution is computed through a linear-time recursion; for costs with bounded curvature density, it is characterized by a scalar ordinary differential equation. The policy achieves expected regret of $O(T^{2/3})$ against the best fixed order in hindsight over $T$ periods. Under independent demand and suitable curvature of expected losses, the bound improves to $O(\sqrt{T})$. Matching minimax lower bounds establish rate optimality over the corresponding classes with a fixed marginal-cost bound. Both rates extend to nonperishable inventory under uniformly positive conditional expected demand. Numerical experiments on synthetic and retail data show improvements over alternative policies using censored observations.
item.dc:creator: Zhengchao Wang, Nam Ho-Nguyen

item.title: Allen--Cahn Residual-Constrained Topology Optimization via an Augmented Lagrangian Method
item.description: arXiv:2611.02375v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents a residual-constrained topology optimization framework that controls interface transition bandwidth without requiring external density filters. The steady conserved Allen--Cahn (AC) equation is formulated as an equality residual constraint and solved via a mass-weighted Augmented Lagrangian Method (ALM) coupled with the Method of Moving Asymptotes (MMA). A closed-form chemical potential projection eliminates the constant residual mode, ensuring algebraic compatibility with external volume targets. Variational sensitivity analysis reveals a symmetric-plus-rank-one Jacobian that yields matrix-free sensitivities without additional adjoint PDE solves, reducing residual sensitivity overhead to only 0.11% of the state elasticity solve time in 3D. Systematic 2D benchmarks confirm that interface bandwidth is governed intrinsically by reaction--diffusion parameters across mesh refinements. While diffuse interfaces incur a continuous compliance elevation (1.4%--12.3%), a volume-preserving 0/1 post-processing audit across 48 benchmark cases demonstrates that this gap stems primarily from intermediate-density penalization: binarized AC-ALM designs achieve equal or superior stiffness in 45 configurations (averaging 1.2% stiffer than SIMP). Simultaneously, single-node hinges and strut fragmentation are substantially suppressed compared to unregularized baselines. Three-dimensional benchmarks further demonstrate practical spatial viability for complex structures.
item.dc:creator: Run Du, Xuan Xiao, Wenming Cheng, Zeqiang Zhang

item.title: Conditional stopping guarantees for a folded parametrization of reduced Stokes vectors
item.description: arXiv:2611.02421v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stopping decisions made in parametrization coordinates need not certify physically accurate estimates. We establish conditional stopping guarantees for a folded parametrization of reduced Stokes vectors, including partial linear polarization. For strongly convex physical objectives on the bounded-intensity inner sheet, normalized first derivatives and one radial lower-curvature test give an explicit objective-gap bound with sharp tolerance orders $\varepsilon^{4/3}+\nu^2$. The guarantee requires neither prior localization near an optimum nor a positive-semidefinite head Hessian. Its information basis is an exact recovery identity: one signed radial curvature restores the physical-gradient component lost at the fully linearly polarized fold, without stationarity or knowledge of the physical Hessian. For a nominal quadratic model, an outward-rounded implementation certifies a gap of at most $10^{-6}$ for 8,861 of 9,284 stored endpoints; it rejects all 295 historical false successes and 128 accurate endpoints. The full 128-fractional-bit pass takes 7.32 seconds and includes 52 scalar curvature evaluations. Controlled fits and released observations distinguish stopping certification from local fold diagnosis and subsequent coordinate repair. Twenty shared-network fits contain no saved near-fold negative-curvature candidates, and direct physical solvers are cheaper on the tested quadratics.
item.dc:creator: Hiroyasu Usami, Ayato Tsuboi, Keisuke Hara

item.title: Subgradient Methods for Nonsmooth Sample Average Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2611.02534v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study direct subgradient methods for nonsmooth sample average approximation (SAA). Subgradient descent and Nesterov acceleration with constant step sizes attain polynomial and geometric rates matching their smooth counterparts. After $O(\log n)$ full-batch updates, where $n$ is the sample size, the computed solution has the same first-order expansion and limiting distribution as an SAA solution, even when the iterates do not converge. A bound on subgradient increments transfers population regularity to the sample objective, controls the algorithmic trajectory, and identifies the leading random term. The bound covers convex piecewise linear scenario costs, including two-stage stochastic linear programs with fixed recourse. Moreau smoothing displaces the population solution at first order and changes the limiting distribution of the computed solution. An explicit shift of the residual removes the first-order displacement and improves the expansion remainder. For sparse decisions, restricted increment bounds give convergence, support recovery, and expansions for proximal subgradient descent and iterative hard thresholding.
item.dc:creator: Xi Chen, Ouqi Fu, Jiyuan Tu, Yichen Zhang

item.title: Stabilization of gravity-capillary water waves with constant vorticity
item.description: arXiv:2611.02570v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish an exponential stabilization result for two-dimensional periodic gravity-capillary water waves of finite depth with constant vorticity, using an external pressure localized on the free surface. The pressure is prescribed as the product of a nonnegative cut-off function and the time derivative of the surface elevation and serves as a feedback control. To prove the main result, we derive the energy dissipation identity and estimate the time integral of the energy relative to the flat Couette flow, by means of the multiplier method and periodic Pohozaev identities. A remaining lower-order term led by the vorticity is removed by a compactness argument based on unique continuation for the linearized equations. Under a condition relating the cut-off to gravity and surface tension, the relative energy decays exponentially on any interval on which a regular solution remains uniformly small in Sobolev norms. We do not assume the evenness on the solution and smallness on the vorticity.
item.dc:creator: Qixing Ding, Jia-Cheng Zhao

item.title: The Staged Pandora's Box: Reservation Indices for Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.02722v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A staged search must decide which candidate to advance next and when to stop. Some observations only inform later decisions; others can be kept as results. We formulate these choices as a staged Pandora's box with a designated set of collectable stages. For independent finite-stage candidates with bounded readings and positive bounded own-history costs, an exact covered-call recursion gives the reservation index, the optimal value and the loss of every advance or stop; advancing an index-maximal candidate while its index exceeds the incumbent is optimal. The representation recovers classical single-stage search, nested inspection and the all-collectable Markov setting, and prices changes in the problem: enlarging the collectable set or lowering costs raises the value by an explicit covered-call overshoot. Resumption can be valuable even when future reward laws do not change, but has no value for deterministic readings. With information sharing across candidates, no rule using only their separate remaining-reading laws is universally optimal, and making an intermediate reading collectable can change which candidate is inspected first. Under a coherent joint path law with own-history costs, an approximate-planning bound controls the recomputed index's regret by changes in untouched candidates' local values; a common-component specialization bounds those changes through predictive total-variation dispersion. Exact finite-law experiments check the representation, the loss accounting and the bounds.
item.dc:creator: Long Vu, Jongseong Brad Choi, Binoy Ravindran, Zhoulai Fu

item.title: Two-point residual step size gradient methods for linear systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.02743v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kaczmarz-type methods often converge slowly when the coefficient matrix is ill-conditioned. In particular, when the smallest singular value is small, every row of the coefficient matrix is nearly orthogonal to the corresponding right singular direction, so that the iteration stalls along that direction. To break this slow-convergence regime, we borrow the delayed-step-size idea of the Barzilai-Borwein (BB) method and, within the framework of the residual-based surrogate-hyperplane Kaczmarz method, propose two new step sizes for gradient-descent-type methods solving linear systems: a delayed residual step size \(\alpha_k^{\mathrm{DR}}\) and a residual-difference step size \(\alpha_k^{\mathrm{RD}}\), which correspond, respectively, to the BB1 and BB2 step sizes in convex quadratic optimization. We prove that \(\alpha_k^{\mathrm{RD}}\le\alpha_k^{\mathrm{DR}}\), and we analyze the convergence of the resulting method in a canonical model with two singular values: although the step sizes are non-monotone, the residual norm is shown to decrease after finitely many steps. Numerical experiments on some ill-conditioned linear systems illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.
item.dc:creator: Xin Xu

item.title: Quasiconvexity and Lower Semicontinuity in the Riemannian Setting
item.description: arXiv:2611.02792v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a notion of quasiconvexity for integrands defined on the bundle of linear maps between the tangent spaces of two smooth, connected and complete Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$ and $(N,h)$, naturally extending the classical Euclidean notion. For continuous integrands, we prove that this Riemannian quasiconvexity is equivalent to the sequential lower semicontinuity of the associated functional $$ F(u,\Omega)=\int_\Omega f(du)\,d\mu_g $$ with respect to the weak$^*$ convergence in $W^{1,\infty}(\Omega,N)$, in the intrinsic sense adopted in the paper, for every bounded open subset $\Omega\subseteq M$. We then establish the Riemannian analogues of the Acerbi--Fusco theorems for Carath\'eodory integrands satisfying the corresponding growth conditions, for every $1\leqslant p\leqslant+\infty$, with respect to the weak and weak$^*$ notions of convergence considered here.
item.dc:creator: Aurora Corbisiero, Chiara Leone, Carlo Mantegazza

item.title: Offline Approximate Value Iteration: A Reinforcement Learning Approach for Satellite Constellation Deployment
item.description: arXiv:2611.02809v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper introduces a reinforcement learning-based approximate dynamic programming approach to optimize the deployment of Walker-type satellite constellations under uncertainties, including launch failures and satellite malfunctions. We formulate the problem as a Markov Decision Process that incorporates low-injection orbit launches, continuous low-thrust orbit raising, and variable satellite loads. We adopt the offline approximate value iteration solution method, using linear function approximation with basis functions and action pruning strategies to substantially reduce the computational and memory requirements for finding optimal decision policies. Preliminary results demonstrate convergence to policies with low expected costs and deployment times, both of which are lower than those of a rolling-horizon baseline, showcasing a novel application of approximate dynamic programming in space logistics.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: 3rd Conference on AI in and for Space (SPAICE 2026), European Space Agency (ESA), Oct 2026, Noordwijk, Netherlands
item.dc:creator: Tristan Leuridan (LGI), Yiping Fang (LGI), Adam Abdin (LGI)

item.title: When Is Tracking Affordable? A Movement-Budget Feasibility Threshold for Dynamic Regret
item.description: arXiv:2611.02812v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dynamic regret measures an online learner against a moving comparator, and standard analyses assume the learner may move freely at every round. We study what happens when it may not: the learner is given a hard budget $S$ on its total movement $\sum_t \|x_t - x_{t-1}\|$. Our main result is that a movement budget creates a feasibility barrier. On a domain of diameter $D$ with $G$-Lipschitz convex losses, for every comparator path length $P_T \in [D, DT]$ we exhibit a deterministic adversary that forces $R_d = \Omega(GDT)$ on every budget-feasible algorithm whenever $S \le c P_T$ for a universal constant $c>0$. This barrier is caused by the budget rather than by a volatile environment: for fixed $D$, it applies when $P_T = o(T)$, where the unconstrained minimax rate $\Theta(G\sqrt{D(D+P_T)T})$ is sublinear, so the same instances are learnable with an unbounded budget and unlearnable without one. Conversely, projected online gradient descent with a budget-aware step size is budget-feasible and attains $o(GDT)$ once $S = \omega(D + P_T)$. Thus the critical movement scale is $D+P_T$: linear regret is unavoidable below a sufficiently small constant multiple of $P_T$, while sublinear regret is achievable when $S/(D+P_T)\to\infty$ in the learnable regime. The construction rests on a distinction we make explicit: what makes a comparator expensive to track under a movement budget is the distance it forces the learner to travel, not its path length. Above the threshold we give a budget-dependent upper bound and identify the tight minimax rate in this region as an open problem rather than claiming a product law. Experiments support the predicted transition location and the $1/S$ decay.
item.dc:creator: Ridham Patel

item.title: Efficient Detailed Scheduling of Multiproduct Pipelines using Action-Decoupled Deep Reinforcement Learning
