item.description: arXiv:2611.02823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multiproduct pipelines transport refined products to delivery stations in sequential batches, and their detailed scheduling must meet market demand while respecting nonlinear hydraulic constraints. Retaining the full hydraulic nonlinearity yields a mixed-integer nonlinear program that is computationally intractable, while the linearization commonly adopted for solver-based optimization degrades hydraulic accuracy without resolving the heavy computational burden. This paper develops an action-decoupled proximal policy optimization (PPO) framework that efficiently produces detailed schedules while preserving hydraulic fidelity. The scheduling process is cast as a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) with flexible action durations. To handle the discrete-continuous hybrid action space, a cascaded dual-actor architecture decouples the discrete operating duration from the continuous flow decisions, eliminating the gradient interference that destabilizes conventional coupled-action policies and thereby yielding high-quality schedules far more efficiently. Validated on a real-world multiproduct pipeline in China and benchmarked against a single-actor baseline and a linearized MILP solved by Gurobi, the proposed framework achieves delivery accuracy close to the exact optimum while substantially improving flow rate stability and substantially reducing solution time.
item.dc:creator: Kai Shao, Ling Jian, Liming Liu, Serguey V. Bogomolov, Xinmin Wang

item.title: A Cooperative Game-Theoretic Framework for Real-Time Deviation Settlement in Local Energy Communities
item.description: arXiv:2611.03030v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper proposes a cooperative game-theoretical framework for the financial settlement of real-time deviations in Community-Based Local Energy Markets (CB-LEMs). The real-time settlement process is modeled as a transferable-utility cooperative game, and the resulting Real-Time Local Energy Market (RTLEM) game is shown to be superadditive and balanced. We analyze two game-theoretical allocation mechanisms, the Shapley value and the nucleolus, and evaluate their efficiency, individual rationality, coalitional rationality, and temporal-aggregation properties. We subsequently compare these mechanisms with a settlement rule based on proportional imbalance responsibility. The three mechanisms are efficient and individually rational, but only the nucleolus is guaranteed to satisfy coalitional rationality for every RTLEM instance. The proposed framework is demonstrated using real-world data from a residential energy community in Amsterdam, showing the trade-offs among the three allocation mechanisms in terms of surplus distribution, coalitional stability, interpretability, and computational requirements.
item.dc:creator: Angel M. Gonz\'alez-Rueda, Iago N\'u\~nez Lugilde, Jose L. Crespo-Vazquez, Tarek Alskaif

item.title: Optimal Configurations for Mordell's Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.03088v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mordell's problem asks for the largest product of squared pairwise distances among $n$ points in the complex plane with a prescribed sum of squared distances from the origin. When this sum equals $n$, the maximum for $2\le n\le5$ is known to be $n^n$, attained precisely by the $n$th roots of unity up to rotation and relabeling. For $n\ge6$, Chalk showed that a regular polygon together with its center gives a larger product than the regular $n$-gon. We prove that for $6\le n\le9$ the maximum is $(n-1)^{n-1}r_n^{n(n-1)}$, where $r_n=\sqrt{n/(n-1)}$. Up to the same symmetries, the unique maximizer consists of the origin and the vertices of a regular $(n-1)$-gon of radius $r_n$. For six points, algebraic elimination reduces the proof to an exact comparison of stationary values. For seven points, we compare all twelve classes in a published classification of equilibria. For eight and nine points, rigorous interval arithmetic establishes an inequality for every admissible pair. Summing over pairs gives the sharp global bound, and the equality conditions determine the configuration. An explicit ten-point comparison and a known instability result together exclude Chalk's configuration for every $n\ge10$. For each $n$ from two through eight, Mordell's problem and the minimum-diameter problem studied by Bateman and Erd\H{o}s have a common optimal configuration.
item.dc:creator: Xiang Ji, Tiancheng Xu, Wensheng Yu

item.title: Diagonal Equivalence in State Space Models: Characterization, Retrieval Rank, and Selective Extensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03101v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify real and complex state-space models (SSMs) with linear transitions, distinguishing fixed-basis diagonal equivalence from input-output equivalence and tracking coefficient-conditioning windows under coordinate changes. We characterize diagonal equivalence through commuting transition families whose members are diagonalizable over the chosen field. With time-shared token-local matrix maps, we identify this class's state-mediated kernels with unnormalized scalar-mode linear attention with multiplicative masks. Mamba 3's multiple-input, multiple-output (MIMO) construction lifts one value per local interface; SSD-MIMO routes independent values for local retrieval rank above one. HybridMamba combines Mamba 1's per-coordinate decay, Mamba 2-style heads and Mamba 3's complex rotations and two-endpoint writes, mixing real and rotating state blocks with different decay laws. They recover Mamba 1-3 single-input, single-output (SISO) configurations as exact special cases. On five large H100 bfloat16 workloads, our fused GPU kernels improve geometric-mean training time over official Mamba 1/3 in matched SISO recoveries, with Mamba 2 near parity at SSM-core scope. Memory tradeoffs depend on the baseline and metric: saved-for-backward versus peak allocation. In small-model multi-token recall experiments, both designs outperform Mamba 1-3 on the hardest tier; higher routing ranks perform best in gated or phase-diverse configurations. In single-seed language models with about 500M parameters, both improve on Mamba 1/2 in test loss at 2B tokens, but the routing gains do not translate into lower language-model loss. Our best configurations approach Mamba 3 SISO through 10B tokens while remaining behind it and Mamba 3 MIMO in language-model loss.
item.dc:creator: Dennis Rochau

item.title: Susceptibility optimization for wisdom of crowds: A social power reformulation and realization framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.03240v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Whether social influence makes a crowd wiser or more biased hinges on who yields to others and who holds firm. Such heterogeneous susceptibilities to social influence, together with the influence network, determine the weight each agent's initial estimate carries in the collective estimate, known as social power. This paper studies susceptibility optimization for maximizing the wisdom of crowds under the Friedkin-Johnsen model. Minimizing the squared collective bias over susceptibilities leads to a nonconvex problem. To overcome this nonconvexity, we develop a social power reformulation and realization framework, which decomposes the problem into two stages: first characterizing the social power that minimizes the collective bias, then determining the susceptibilities that induce such social power. Social power reformulation yields a quadratic program over the probability simplex. Under uniform-sign biases, the optimal social power concentrates on the least biased agents and immediately determines the optimal susceptibilities; under mixed-sign biases, its geometry enables a linear-time construction algorithm. For social power realization, we introduce the notions of susceptibility realizability and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for them, under which we derive all optimal susceptibilities in closed form using the Laplacian pseudoinverse and eigenvector centrality. These results yield a unified algorithm that solves the original problem globally, with worst-case complexity cubic in the number of agents when realizability holds. Finally, we develop a fully distributed implementation with linear communication complexity, illustrating how collective intelligence can emerge from local interactions.
item.dc:creator: Ye Tian, Anzhi Sheng, Angela Fontan, Long Wang, Karl H. Johansson

item.title: On a Class of Non-Local Elliptic-Transport Systems in Score-Guided Probability Flow on $SE(3)$: Score-Singularity Resolution, Space-Time ADN Shift, and Markov Mean-Field Games
item.description: arXiv:2611.03278v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish mathematical foundations for optimal spatiotemporal vector fields governing continuous score-guided probability flows over bounded submanifolds $M \subset SE(3)$ on the Special Euclidean group $SE(3) \cong \mathbb{R}^3 \times SO(3)$. Modeling dynamic density evolution via a score-perturbed Lie-algebraic continuity equation under zero-flux boundary conditions, we resolve the non-local score drift singularity $s(g,t) = \nabla_{SE(3)} \log \rho(g,t)$ as $\rho \rightarrow 0^+$ via weighted parabolic flux dissipation bounds. Using left-invariant exponential group mollifiers, we derive boundary-preserving DiPerna--Lions commutator estimates tracking structure constants $\{c_{ij}^k\}$. Second, interpreting the optimality system as a 7D space-time elliptic operator $L_{7D} = -\Delta_{SE(3)} - \partial_t^2$ with zero-order corner compatibility on $\partial M \times \{0,T\}$, we establish Agmon--Douglis--Nirenberg $W_p^2(Q_T)$ shift estimates tracking Lie algebra constants, boundary geometry $\|\partial M\|_{C^2}$, and Ricci curvature $\|Ric_{SE(3)}\|_{L^\infty}$, yielding a full $C^\infty(\overline{Q}_T)$ Schauder bootstrap expansion. Third, we extend this system to non-cooperative Markov Mean-Field Games (MFGs) on $SE(3)$, establishing score-guided Nash equilibria via Schauder--Tychonoff fixed points. Crucially, the constant diagonal Ricci curvature $Ric_{SE(3)} = \mathrm{diag}(0,0,0,1/2,1/2,1/2)$ from $SO(3)$ induces a sharp Bochner--Weitzenb\"ock spectral gap boost $\lambda_1(-\Delta_{SE(3)}) \ge \lambda_1(-\Delta_{\mathbb{R}^3}) + 1/2 > 0$. This positive rotational curvature enhances the Lie-algebraic Poincar\'e coercivity constant, demonstrating that intrinsic group curvature stabilizes score-guided flows against dispersion and expands the critical Nash uniqueness horizon $T_{SE(3)}^*$ beyond flat Euclidean limits.
item.dc:creator: Pilhwa Lee

item.title: First- and second-order constrained optimisation for inverse homogenisation of unidirectionally varying microstructure
item.description: arXiv:2611.03372v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper is concerned with inverse homogenisation problems that aim to identify microstructure features of a body from macroscopic measurements. The unknown microstructure is assumed to vary macroscopically in one spatial direction and affects the effective tensor in an elliptic partial differential equation that governs the behaviour of the body on the macroscale. We establish the well-posedness of the PDE-constrained minimisation problems that model the task of identifying the microstructure, derive first-order necessary optimality conditions, and prove the convergence of a gradient-projection algorithm for the studied problem class in an infinite-dimensional setting. We moreover demonstrate that recently obtained results on generalised differentiability properties of solution maps of bilateral obstacle problems make it possible to set up and analyse a novel semismooth Newton method in the considered situation. The functional analytic setting that we use for our investigation is chosen such that it covers various elliptic PDEs simultaneously (classical second-order equations, bi-Laplace problems, linear elasticity, etc.) and explicitly exploits the problem structure to obtain global convergence guarantees for the studied solution algorithms in terms of the Lipschitz constants of the involved operators. Our analysis is accompanied by numerical experiments which show that the new semismooth Newton approach requires far less expensive projection evaluations than the gradient-descent method and, thus, offers a significant speedup.
item.dc:creator: Constantin Christof, Malte A. Peter, Michael Ulbrich

item.title: Open problems from the Length Optimization event at MDS 2026
item.description: arXiv:2611.03403v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: During the Minisymposium on Length Optimization as part of the International Conference "Mathematics Days in Sofia - 2026", the participants collected the following open problems: 1. Find any non-trivial upper and lower bounds for the degree of a branching point in the Gilbert-Steiner problem with cost-function $c(x) = x^p$ in the metric space $X = \mathbb{R}^d$ for large $d$ and fixed $p > 1/2$ (see Section 1). 2. Determine whether a typical trajectory of a given branched optimal traffic plan has bounded length. To find the optimal transport plan between the Dirac measure in the center of a circle and the Lebesgue measure on the circle (see Section 2). 3. To find the maximal distance minimizers for any explicit compact sets (see Section 3). 4. What is the minimal $C$ such that for any set of $n$ points in the three-dimensional unit cube, there is a tour through all these $n$ points with the sum of the cubes of its edge lengths at most $C$ (see Section 4). 5. To explore parallels between tropical caustics and Steiner trees: do caustics really need convexity (see Section 5).
item.dc:creator: Yana Teplitskaya

item.title: A Bayesian Framework for Safe Optimal Control of Unknown Systems from Input-Output Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.03466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As control engineering is applied to increasingly complex systems, learning-based control, which uses empirical data to reduce the reliance on first-principles models, has emerged as a promising paradigm. However, such approaches must cope with nonlinear and stochastic dynamics, the absence of state measurements, and scarce data, while ensuring safe operation under constraints, which requires rigorous uncertainty quantification. Whereas existing methods treat these challenges in isolation, this article proposes a Bayesian framework that jointly addresses them. A prior in state-space form is updated from input-output data using particle Markov chain Monte Carlo methods, yielding a representation of joint uncertainty over dynamics and latent states. Building on this representation, a validation procedure is developed that provides probabilistic guarantees for constraint satisfaction under arbitrary causal control laws. For control synthesis, a formulation penalizing the conditional value-at-risk of the constraint function is proposed, together with an adaptive calibration mechanism that adjusts the performance-robustness trade-off to achieve a desired robustness level. The probability of successful certification is characterized theoretically. The framework is extended to a receding-horizon setting, where posterior updates from new measurements allow the controller to progressively reduce uncertainty and improve performance. The approach is demonstrated on the optimal control of a vertical farm.
item.dc:creator: Robert Lefringhausen, Annalena Daniels, Michael Fink, Sandra Hirche

item.title: Tilted Convexity and an Exact Offline-Online Separation
item.description: arXiv:2611.03472v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Convexity has three equivalent descriptions: support by affine functions, monotonicity of the subdifferential, and increasing secant slopes. We weaken all three by one distortion with parameter $\gamma\in(0,1]$, which multiplies positive changes by $\gamma$ and divides negative ones by $\gamma$. The resulting classes are the convex functions at $\gamma=1$ and, for $\gamma<1$, are distinct and nested, with the parameter dropping by at most a square along the chain. For proper lower semicontinuous functions in these classes, the effective domain is convex, local minimizers are global, and the function is locally Lipschitz on the relative interior of its domain. The classes separate offline from online optimization over compact convex sets with efficient projection, with access to function values and bounded support vectors. A smooth member of any class can be minimized to additive accuracy $\varepsilon$ with $\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon)$ first-order queries and projections. Online, with nonpositive losses and $\alpha$-regret measured against $\alpha$ times the best fixed point, a polynomial-time algorithm achieves $\gamma$-regret $O(\sqrt T)$ on the largest class. For every fixed, effectively specified $\gamma\in(0,1)$ and every $\alpha\in(\gamma,1]$, no randomized polynomial-time algorithm has sublinear expected $\alpha$-regret unless $\mathbf{NP}=\mathbf{RP}$, already for smooth concave polynomial losses in the smallest class, each minimized by one linear optimization. Thus, unless $\mathbf{NP}=\mathbf{RP}$, $\gamma$ is the exact online coefficient of each class, while the offline coefficient is one.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Pedramfar, Rajiv Khanna, Christopher John Quinn, Vaneet Aggarwal

item.title: Delay-Certified Readiness Barriers for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation Without Lipschitz Constants
item.description: arXiv:2611.03490v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Overactuated multirotors can produce the same wrench with many rotor-speed combinations, some of which leave the vehicle unable to change its wrench quickly, e.g., to reject a gust. Readiness barriers keep this ability, the readiness, above a floor, but only in continuous time; with sampled commands and varying speed-controller delays, the available robustness bound covers less than one millisecond. We remove this limit by exploiting the structure of the problem: each rotor responds monotonically and in closed form to its own torque, so the speeds reachable under uncertain switching times lie in a cheaply computed box, and the lowest readiness over that box sits at a corner known in advance. This yields a Lipschitz-free test that a command keeps the readiness above its floor until the next sample, plus a fallback torque that keeps the vehicle on a certified plan. In hexarotor simulations with 2--40~ms delays and $\pm2$~ms jitter, the filter never violated the floor. At $10\pm2$~ms, it matched a delay-compensating predictor within the design envelope and cost 2--30\% more tracking error beyond it, where the predictor alone violated the floor in 2 to 16 of 16 missions.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Silano

item.title: Online Matching with Arbitrary Stochastic Rewards
item.description: arXiv:2611.03598v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online matching with stochastic rewards is a generalization of online bipartite matching in which an attempt to match an online arrival to an offline resource may fail with some probability. Each arrival allows at most one attempt and the success probabilities of its edges are revealed when it arrives. Greedy is 0.5-competitive, which is the best possible for deterministic algorithms. While better competitive ratios are known in several special cases, beating 0.5 for arbitrary probabilities has remained open. We show that, against the adaptive offline benchmark and for arbitrary probabilities, a randomized Perturbed Greedy algorithm is at least 0.591-competitive in the unweighted setting and at least 0.531-competitive with vertex weights. The perturbation functions combine Greedy with scaled versions of the classic exponential function.
item.dc:creator: Rajan Udwani

item.title: Multi-Trajectory Parallel-in-Iteration Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.03621v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Previously, we developed a ``parallel-in-iteration'' optimization framework that uses multigrid reduction-in-time (MGRIT) to parallelize slowly converging optimization methods, such as gradient descent. Unlike time-dependent evolution problems, optimization requires only a final point with a sufficiently small gradient, rather than an accurate approximation of the entire trajectory of iterates. This motivates a different use of MGRIT: instead of repeatedly improving the approximation of a single long trajectory, we introduce restarted MGRIT (R-MGRIT), which performs one MGRIT iteration on a trajectory, takes the approximate final point as a new initial guess, and repeats the process on a new trajectory. Each restart thus defines a new all-at-once system, allowing progress toward the solution without accurately approximating the preceding trajectory. Moreover, we find that these trajectories can be shortened without increasing the number of restarts needed for convergence. We provide theoretical results comparing MGRIT and R-MGRIT for linear problems and demonstrate the convergence behavior of the shortened trajectories numerically for both linear and nonlinear problems. Shortening the trajectories increases the estimated parallel speedup while reducing the number of processors required.
item.dc:creator: Guilherme H. M. Araujo, Oliver A. Krzysik, Hans De Sterck

item.title: Optimal Control of Stationary Doubly Diffusive Flows in Bounded Lipschitz Domains: Analysis and Numerical Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2308.02178v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we study the control constrained distributed optimal control of a stationary doubly diffusive flow model. For the control problem, we use a well-posedness analysis based on minimal assumptions on data and domain. We show the existence of an optimal control with quadratic type cost functional, study the Fr\'echet differentiability properties of the control-to-state map and establish the first-order necessary optimality conditions corresponding to the optimal control problem. Expanding on this we prove the local optimality of a reference control using second-order sufficient optimality condition for the control problem. Then, following the \textit{optimize-then-discretize} approach, we propose a fully non-conforming, locally exactly divergence-free discretization of the control problem based on the lowest order $(\texttt{CR}_0, \mathbb{P}_0)$ finite element spaces for the state and adjoint variables, and explicit and implicit discretizations for the control variable. Optimal \textit{a priori} error estimates are established for the state, adjoint and control variables in suitable norms up to the regularity of the solution. Finally, the optimal control is computed using a primal-dual active set strategy as a semi-smooth Newton method and numerical experiments are performed to validate the theoretical findings, and it's applicability to optimal control of thermal and solutal convection in a porous medium.
item.dc:creator: Jai Tushar, Arbaz Khan, Manil T. Mohan

item.title: Learning to Select Between LP and SDP Relaxations for Nonconvex Quadratically Constrained Quadratic Programs
item.description: arXiv:2501.03954v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quadratically constrained quadratic programs (QCQPs) are ubiquitous in optimization: Such problems arise in applications from operations research, power systems, signal processing, chemical engineering, and portfolio theory, among others. Despite their flexibility in modeling real-life situations and the recent effort to understand their properties, nonconvex QCQPs are hard to solve in practice. Most of the approaches in the literature are based on either Linear Programming (LP) or Semidefinite Programming (SDP) relaxations, each of which works very well for some problem subclasses but perform poorly on others. In this paper, we develop a relaxation selection procedure for nonconvex QCQPs that can adaptively decide whether an LP- or SDP-based approach is expected to be more beneficial by considering the instance structure. The proposed methodology relies on utilizing machine learning methods that involve features derived from spectral properties and sparsity patterns of data matrices, and once trained appropriately within a dimension-independent setup, the prediction model applies to any instance with an arbitrary number of variables and constraints. We develop classification and regression models under different feature-design setups, including a dimension-independent representation, and evaluate them on synthetically generated instances and a combined benchmark dataset consisting of MINLPLib and QPLIB instances. We further investigate relaxation selection within a spatial branch-and-bound framework, evaluating the trade-off between lower bound quality and computational time.
item.dc:creator: Muge Dedeoglu, Buket Ozen, Burak Kocuk

item.title: A SPIDER-type stochastic subgradient method for expectation-constrained nonconvex nonsmooth optimization
item.description: arXiv:2501.19214v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many real-world problems, such as those with fairness constraints, involve complex expectation constraints and large datasets, necessitating the design of efficient stochastic methods to solve them. Most existing research focuses on cases with no {constraint} or easy-to-project constraints or deterministic constraints. In this paper, we consider nonconvex nonsmooth stochastic optimization problems with expectation constraints, for which we build a novel exact penalty model. We first show the relationship between the penalty model and the original problem. Then on solving the penalty problem, we present a single-loop SPIDER-type stochastic subgradient method, which utilizes the subgradients of both the objective and constraint functions, as well as the constraint function value at each iteration. Under certain regularity conditions (weaker than Slater-type constraint qualification or strong feasibility assumed in existing works), we establish an iteration complexity result of $O(\epsilon^{-4})$ to reach a near-$\epsilon$ stationary point of the penalized problem in expectation, matching the lower bound for such tasks. Building on the exact penalization, an $(\epsilon,\epsilon)$-KKT point of the original problem is obtained. For a few scenarios, our complexity of either the {objective} sample subgradient or the constraint sample function values can be lower than the state-of-the-art results by a factor of $\epsilon^{-2}$. Moreover, on solving two fairness-constrained problems and a multi-class Neyman-Pearson classification problem, our method is significantly (up to 466 times) faster than the state-of-the-art algorithms, including switching subgradient method and inexact proximal point methods.
item.dc:creator: Wei Liu, Yangyang Xu

item.title: Accelerated Gradient Methods Through Variable and Operator Splitting
item.description: arXiv:2505.04065v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This survey develops a variable and operator splitting (VOS) framework for accelerated first-order methods. Operator splitting separates the components of the optimality system, while variable splitting introduces auxiliary dynamics that generate acceleration. The strong Lyapunov property guides the stability analysis, and practical schemes follow from Accelerated Over-Relaxation (AOR) and Extrapolation by Predictor--Corrector (EPC) discretizations. For merely convex problems, a perturbed VOS flow combined with homotopy in the auxiliary scale yields accelerated rates. The framework gives a common derivation and analysis of Nesterov-type, FISTA-type, composite, mirror-descent-type, and bilinear saddle-point accelerated methods. Its main contribution is structural and expository: it organizes these methods within one Lyapunov and splitting template and explains how acceleration survives different splittings and discretizations.
item.dc:creator: Long Chen, Luo Hao, Jingrong Wei

item.title: A Learning-Based Inexact ADMM for Solving Quadratic Programs
item.description: arXiv:2505.09391v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Convex quadratic programs (QPs) constitute a fundamental computational primitive across diverse domains including financial optimization, control systems, and machine learning. The alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) has emerged as a preferred first-order approach due to its iteration efficiency - exemplified by the state-of-the-art OSQP solver. Machine learning-enhanced optimization algorithms have recently demonstrated significant success in speeding up the solving process. This work introduces a neural-accelerated ADMM variant that replaces exact subproblem solutions with learned approximations through a parameter-efficient Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network. We derive convergence guarantees within the inexact ADMM formalism, establishing that our learning-augmented method maintains primal-dual convergence while satisfying residual thresholds. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves superior solution accuracy compared to existing learning-based methods while delivering significant computational speedups of up to $7\times$, $28\times$, and $22\times$ over Gurobi, SCS, and OSQP, respectively. Furthermore, the proposed method outperforms other learning-to-optimize methods in terms of solution quality. Detailed performance analysis confirms near-perfect compliance with the theoretical assumptions, consequently ensuring algorithm convergence.
item.dc:creator: Xi Gao, Jinxin Xiong, Linxin Yang, Akang Wang, Weiwei Xu, Jiang Xue

item.title: Radial Epiderivative Based Fritz John and KKT Conditions in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2509.01272v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this study, we examine Fritz John (FJ) and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) type optimality conditions for a class of nonsmooth and nonconvex optimization problems with inequality constraints, where the objective and constraint functions all are assumed to be radially epidifferentiable. The concept of the radial epiderivative constitutes a distinct generalization of classical derivative notions, as it replaces the conventional limit operation with an infimum-based construction. This formulation permits the analysis of directional behavior without invoking standard neighborhood-based assumptions and constructions commonly required in generalized differentiation. This leads to one of the key advantages of the radial epiderivative which lies in its applicability even to discrete domains, where classical and generalized derivatives are often inapplicable or undefined. The other advantage of this concept is that it provides a possibility to inverstigate KKT conditions for global minimums. Consequently, this approach necessitates a reformulation of fundamental analytical tools such as gradient vectors, feasible direction sets, constraint qualifications and other concepts which are central to the derivation of optimality conditions in smooth optimization theory. The primary contribution of this paper is the development of a comprehensive theoretical framework for KKT conditions tailored to the radially epidifferentiable setting. We introduce novel definitions of the radial gradient vector, of the set of feasible directions, and examine how classical constraint qualifications may be interpreted and extended within this new framework.
item.dc:creator: Refail Kasimbeyli, Jian-Wen Peng, Jen-Chih Yao

item.title: Clapping: Removing Per-sample Storage for Pipeline Parallel Distributed Optimization with Communication Compression
item.description: arXiv:2509.19029v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pipeline-parallel distributed optimization is essential for large-scale machine learning but is challenged by significant communication overhead from transmitting high-dimensional activations and gradients between workers. Existing approaches often depend on impractical unbiased gradient assumptions or incur sample-size memory overhead. This paper introduces Clapping, a Communication compression algorithm with LAzy samPling for Pipeline-parallel learnING. Clapping adopts a lazy sampling strategy that reuses data samples across steps, breaking sample-wise memory barrier and supporting convergence in few-epoch or online regimes. Clapping comprises two variants including Clapping-FC and Clapping-FU, both of which achieve convergence without unbiased assumption for compressed gradient, effectively addressing compression error propagation in multi-worker settings. Numerical experiments validate the performance of Clapping across different tasks.
item.dc:creator: Boao Kong, Xu Huang, Yuqi Xu, Yixuan Liang, Bin Wang, Kun Yuan

item.title: Constrained Mean Field Games with Grushin type dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2602.12807v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is devoted to a class of finite horizon deterministic mean field games with Grushin type dynamics, state constraints and nonlocal coupling. First, we consider the optimal control problem that each agent aims to solve when the evolution of the population is given and we establish some properties as: the existence of an optimal trajectory for any starting point $(x,t)$, the closed graph property for the multivalued map which associates to each point $(x,t)$ the set of optimal trajectories starting from that point, endowed with a suitable notion of convergence, the continuity of the value function. The main issue to overcome is due to the local interplay at boundary points between the set of state constraints and the degenerate dynamics. To this end, we shall point out two different sets of assumptions which are both sufficient for these properties. Afterwards, we tackle the mean field games; taking advantage of the aforementioned properties, we prove the existence of a relaxed equilibrium (which describes the evolution of the game in terms of a probability on the set of admissible trajectories) and derive the existence of a mild solution (which is a couple formed by the value function for the generic player and a family of time dependent measures on the state).
item.dc:creator: Alessandra Cutr\`i, Paola Mannucci, Claudio Marchi, Nicoletta Tchou

item.title: Inexact Bregman Sparse Newton Method for Efficient Optimal Transport
item.description: arXiv:2603.07156v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Computing exact optimal transport (OT) distances at large scale remains computationally challenging. Entropy-regularized OT can be solved efficiently, but its solution is biased toward the regularized problem, and small regularization parameters often lead to slow convergence and numerical instability. In this paper, we propose \emph{Inexact Bregman Sparse Newton} (IBSN), an efficient method for high-accuracy computation of the original OT problem. Building on a verifiable inexact Bregman proximal framework, IBSN develops a sparse Newton inner solver tailored to the semi-dual formulation, which yields a lower-dimensional Newton system. To accelerate the inner subproblem solves, we introduce a Hessian sparsification strategy tailored to the semi-dual formulation, which reduces the cost of Newton direction computation while preserving key spectral properties. We establish convergence guarantees for the resulting algorithm, including convergence of the inner sparse Newton iterations and global convergence of the overall method to an optimal OT solution. Numerical experiments on synthetic and real datasets show that IBSN is effective in high-accuracy regimes and compares favorably with representative first-order and second-order OT solvers.
item.dc:creator: Jianting Pan, Ji'an Li, Sirong Dai, Ming Yan

item.title: Fixed-Point Delayed Subgradient Methods for Nonsmooth Convex Optimization Problems
item.description: arXiv:2603.19604v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we consider the nonsmooth convex optimization problems over the fixed point constraint sets of firmly nonexpansive operators. To find an optimal solution of the problem, we present an iterative method based on the hybrid steepest descent method and the idea of a delayed subgradient scheme in which allows the use of staled subgradients from the earlier iteration when updating the next iteration. We start the convergence part by deriving an upper bound for the difference of the best-achieved function values and the optimal value. After that, to ensure the convergence in iterations, we prove that there exists a subsequence of the generated sequence by the proposed method which converges to an optimal solution. Moreover, we subsequently show that the whole generated sequence converges to an optimal solution when the strict convexity of the objective function is imposed. Further, we extend the presented results to the inexact version and the centralized network system consisting of a finite number of workers and a central server. Finally, we apply the proposed method to image inpainting problems. The numerical results describe the effect of delay in many cases of objective functions.
item.dc:creator: Ontima Pankoon, Nimit Nimana, Yeol Je Cho

item.title: Piecewise M-Stationarity and Convergence of a Bounding Algorithm for Mathematical Programs with Complementarity Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2603.23389v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This study explores B-stationarity condition for mathematical programs with complementarity constraints (MPCCs) and convergence of a Bounding Algorithm we proposed in [33]. Special attention is given to the cases with biactive complementarity constraints. First, we introduce the concept of piecewise M-stationarity and prove its equivalence to B-stationarity under MPCC-GCQ. Then, this concept is employed to propose a simplified B-stationarity verifica- tion. Finally, we investigate improved convergence properties of the Bounding Algorithm in [33]. Limit points of this method are shown to be C-stationary, based on the stationarity of an approaching sequence; moreover, they are piece-wise M-stationary (and therefore B-stationary), if an additional second-order condition is satisfied by the sequence.
item.dc:creator: Kexin Wang, Lorenz T. Biegler

item.title: New Characterizations of Nonsmooth Convex Functions via Generalized Derivatives
item.description: arXiv:2603.24951v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies the convexity properties of nonsmooth extended-real-valued weakly convex functions, a class of functions that is central to modern optimization and its applications. We establish new characterizations of convexity using second-order generalized derivative tools, including subgradient graphical derivatives, second subderivatives, and second-order subdifferentials. These tools allow us to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for convexity in the nonsmooth framework.
item.dc:creator: Vo Thanh Phat

item.title: Continuum-marginal optimal transport: a mesh-free kernel method
item.description: arXiv:2604.24226v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we study continuum-marginal optimal transport. Given a time-continuous family of probability marginals, the problem is to recover the minimum-energy velocity field whose flow reproduces every marginal. This problem is the continuum limit of the classical two-marginal Benamou-Brenier formulation, and also the deterministic limit of the Nelson problem of stochastic optimal transport. We propose a practical mesh-free solver for this problem. The weak continuity equation is embedded in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, yielding a sample-only objective that requires no spatial discretization. The velocity is parametrized by any linear-in-parameters dictionary or neural network, and is optimized by mini-batch stochastic methods. Synthetic experiments confirm that the method achieves accurate drift recovery and marginal consistency. The same computational framework also applies to the Nelson problem.
item.dc:creator: Yumiharu Nakano

item.title: Muon with Nesterov Momentum: Heavy-Tailed Noise and (Randomized) Inexact Polar Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2605.06884v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Most first-order optimizers treat matrix-valued parameters as vectors, ignoring the intrinsic geometry of hidden-layer weights in neural networks. Muon addresses this mismatch by updating along the polar factor of a momentum matrix, but its theoretical understanding has lagged behind practice. In particular, practical implementations incorporate Nesterov momentum, compute the polar factor only approximately, and operate with stochastic gradients that may be heavy-tailed. We close this gap by developing a convergence theory for Muon with Nesterov momentum and inexact polar decomposition in non-convex matrix optimization under heavy-tailed noise. Our analysis builds on a unified framework for inexact polar decomposition that captures practical iterative approximations such as Newton-Schulz and quantifies how their errors propagate through the optimization dynamics. Under uniform bounds on polar errors, we establish an optimal iteration and sample complexity of $O \left(\varepsilon^{\frac{-(3\alpha-2)}{(\alpha-1)}} \right)$ for finding an $\varepsilon$-stationary point, where $\alpha\in(1,2]$~denotes the heavy-tail index. For the inexact-polar setting with $\sigma_1=0$, we also provide guarantees that do not require prior knowledge of $\alpha$. We analyze a randomized low-rank polar decomposition that is substantially more efficient than full-space methods while remaining compatible with our theory. Numerical experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed inexact and randomized~variants.
item.dc:creator: Sayantan Choudhury, Xiaoran Cheng, Martin Tak\'a\v{c}, Sen Na, Mladen Kolar

item.title: Lifted Schr\"odinger Bridges for Gaussian Mixture Endpoints: Projection Gaps and Path-Space Obstructions
item.description: arXiv:2605.24795v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study stochastic density control between Gaussian-mixture endpoint distributions under Brownian prior dynamics. Since the direct Schr\"odinger bridge between Gaussian mixtures is generally not available in closed form, we introduce a lifted path-space construction in which each trajectory is augmented with a source--target component label. Consequently, the problem decomposes into Gaussian component-to-component Schr\"odinger bridges with explicit marginal, drift, and cost formulas, while the mixture-level assignment reduces to a finite-dimensional entropic coupling problem with a Sinkhorn scaling form. We then analyze the projection obtained by discarding or forgetting the label. By construction, the projected law satisfies the original Gaussian-mixture endpoint constraints, but its relative entropy generally differs from the lifted relative entropy by a nonnegative conditional label-information gap. This gap reveals a path-space obstruction: the lifted optimizer cannot, in general, be identified with the direct unlabeled Schr\"odinger bridge after projection. We also derive the posterior-averaged Markov drift associated with the projected marginal flow, prove a kinetic-energy upper bound, and identify a common path-potential condition under which the projection gap vanishes. Several numerical illustrations showing density and shape control are recorded for a self-contained exposition.
item.dc:creator: Siddhartha Ganguly, George Rapakoulias, Panagiotis Tsiotras

item.title: Accelerating Sinkhorn for Entropy-Regularized Optimal Transport
item.description: arXiv:2605.30267v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Entropy-regularized optimal transport is widely used to compare and align data distributions, but Sinkhorn can converge slowly at small regularization. We introduce Acc-Sinkhorn, a two-state Hessian-driven Nesterov iteration built on the dual mirror geometry of the row-reduced Sinkhorn map. The method combines momentum acceleration with an inexpensive descent safeguard, sta- ble log-domain evaluation, and a prescribed homotopy schedule requiring neither line search nor curvature estimation. We prove global linear convergence of the safeguarded method, rule out con- secutive restarts, and establish local accelerated convergence for fixed parameters without restarts through spectral analysis. Numerical comparisons with six methods on synthetic problems, color transfer, and bilingual word alignment show runtime speedups of up to about 26 over Sinkhorn, with additional rendering-accuracy comparisons for color transfer.
item.dc:creator: Long Chen, Zeyi Xu

item.title: L2-L2-gain bounds for quadratic output systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.00552v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive an explicit bound for the L2-L2-gain of linear time-invariant systems whose output is a quadratic function of the state and the input. Such systems appear naturally in many areas, for example for port-Hamiltonian systems, optimal-control, and stochastic problems. In case the output is purely quadratic in the state, the bound is determined by the supremum over $\omega\in\mathbb R$ of the L2-norms of the bivariate transfer function restricted to the anti-diagonals $\{(s,\, i\omega-s)\mid s\in i\mathbb R\}$ of the frequency domain $i\mathbb R\times i\mathbb R $. Further, we show how the bound can be computed by solving linear matrix equations. This result provides a practical tool for assessing and reducing quadratic-output models.
item.dc:creator: Birgit Hillebrecht

item.title: Mean Field Reinforcement Learning: Theory and Algorithms for Mean Field Control
item.description: arXiv:2607.01525v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This monograph provides an introduction to mean field reinforcement learning through the lens of Markov decision processes arising from large-population stochastic control with mean field interactions and common noise. Starting from the connection between multi-agent reinforcement learning and mean field control, it develops the probabilistic, mathematical, and control-theoretic framework needed to formulate representative-agent learning problems, analyze their relationship with finite-population systems, and study both general and linear-quadratic models. The presentation includes dynamic programming principles, propagation-of-chaos limits, and theoretical analyses of tabular Q-learning and policy-gradient methods. It also discusses numerical implementations, including tabular schemes and deep reinforcement learning methods such as deep deterministic policy gradient. The goal is to give readers a coherent bridge between mean field control theory and reinforcement learning methodology, emphasizing the mathematical structure of the problems and the design of tractable learning approaches for large stochastic populations.
item.dc:creator: Ren\'e Carmona, Mathieu Lauri\`ere

item.title: Adaptive Schauder Stochastic Mirror Descent in Banach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.13121v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we solve risk functional minimization problems with general losses in Banach spaces within the framework of stochastic approximation. We introduce an adaptive regularization strategy for stochastic mirror descent (SMD). Specifically, using a Schauder basis, we construct nested finite-dimensional subspaces whose dimensions adapt to the sample size $n$ to balance approximation and optimization errors. We solve each SMD subproblem over the corresponding subspace and project the stochastic subgradient onto its dual space. This yields closed-form solutions and coordinate-wise coefficient updates with low computational and storage complexity. For risk minimization in $\mathcal{L}^p$ spaces with $1<p<\infty$, we construct Bregman distances adapted to the uniform convexity of the underlying Banach space using $\max\{2,p\}$-convex functionals. At the $\mathcal{L}^1$ endpoint, we instead construct a locally strongly convex functional based on the entropy function. By developing a new analytical framework, we show that the risk functional values converge to the minimum at a rate of $\mathcal{O}\left(n^{-\min\{\frac12,\frac1p\}}\right)$, up to logarithmic factors. In the misspecified setting, we prove convergence under weaker regularity assumptions and derive explicit polynomial rates under suitable regularity conditions. Finally, we apply the method to statistical inverse problems and illustrate its empirical performance through numerical experiments in both settings.
item.dc:creator: Jinhui Bai, Shuai Lu, Lei Shi

item.title: On the Local Linear Convergence of Operator Splitting Methods for Conic Programming
item.description: arXiv:2608.16054v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Operator-splitting methods such as the primal-dual hybrid gradient method (PDHG) and the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) often exhibit linear convergence on conic programs, although general theory guarantees only sublinear rates. We identify two geometric conditions -- strict complementarity and quadratic facial violation -- that explain this local behavior: under these conditions, PDHG and ADMM converge linearly to an optimal solution when initialized sufficiently close to the converging strictly complementary solution. We establish this result through a unified and verifiable primal-dual error-bound framework. First, we show that strict complementarity, together with a quadratic facial-violation property of the associated complementary faces, implies uniform quadratic growth of both the primal and dual augmented Lagrangians near a strictly complementary solution. Second, we prove the local equivalence of three regularity conditions: uniform quadratic growth of the augmented Lagrangians, quadratic growth of a localized smoothed primal-dual gap, and metric subregularity of the saddle-point mapping. This equivalence clarifies the relationship among previously proposed conditions for local linear convergence. Third, using a unified formulation, we give a concise analysis showing that these equivalent conditions yield local linear convergence of PDHG and ADMM. We verify the quadratic facial-violation property for standard polyhedral and symmetric cones, as well as relevant faces of exponential and power cones, and show that it is preserved under Cartesian products. We also obtain an improved local rate using a restarted Halpern scheme. Finally, we extend the framework to convex composite optimization through a quadratic subdifferential-violation condition, which generalizes the quadratic facial-violation.
item.dc:creator: Lijun Ding, Haihao Lu, Jinwen Yang

item.title: MOE-DGSCND: Multi-Objective Enterprise Green Supply Chain Network Design
item.description: arXiv:2609.11971v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper introduces and studies the Multi-Objective Enterprise Doubly-Green Supply Chain Network Design (MOE-DGSCND) problem, an extension of Multi-Objective Supply Chain Network Design. The problem studied here is a three-objective combinatorial optimization problem that simultaneously minimizes total cost f1, carbon dioxide emissions f2 and customer dissatisfaction f3 over binary decisions regarding which distribution centers to open and how to assign customer zones to open facilities. The problem generalizes the capacitated facility location problem (CFLP) and is known to be NP-hard (Garey and Johnson, 1979). This paper formally specifies the decision variables, objective functions and constraints and investigates three solution approaches using a single numerical instance: (A) an exact weighted-sum integer linear programming (ILP) formulation solved with Python combinatorially and via PuLP, (B) three Fully Polynomial-Time Approximation Schemes (FPTAS) providing (1 + $\epsilon$)-approximate solutions for $\epsilon$ := 0.15 and (C) two baseline heuristics for comparison. On an instance with eight customers and five candidate distribution centers, the exact solver certifies the optimal (sampled) supported solutions across eight weight combinations, while the FPTAS-based approaches complete within milliseconds, compared to centiseconds for the exact ILP on this tiny non-stochastic instance.
item.dc:creator: Felix Reichel

item.title: Excitation and Identifiability in the 2D Navier-Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2609.31230v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Convergence in parameter estimation classically requires ``persistency of excitation," which is a non-degeneracy condition on a trajectory-dependent signal. To the best of our knowledge, this paper develops the first such excitation theory for a nonlinear PDE. In the context of identifying the unknown viscosity from spectral observations in the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations for incompressible fluids, our excitation condition is computable, verifiable a priori, and sharp with respect to scaling. Our approach employs a data assimilation methodology to account for an unknown initial state and select candidate viscosities by minimizing the loss between the observed low-modes of the fluid velocity and low-modes of a nudging-based filter assimilating these observations. The main novelty of our framework is to distinguish a new functional, $\mathsf{W}$, representing the work done by the filter's associated sensitivity variable on the enstrophy, around which our entire analysis is centered. We show that $\mathsf{W}$ is explicitly comparable to the observability Gramian of the associated Gauss--Newton iteration, and subsequently establish the following dichotomy at every critical point of the observational loss: either $\mathsf{W}$ exceeds a minimal excitation threshold, in which case the candidate viscosity obeys an explicit error estimate that depends inversely on $\mathsf{W}$ and the observational density $N$, but directly on the error between initial conditions, or else the observations are quantitatively insensitive to parameter updates in a way that is detectable to the user. Our approach is energy-based, and therefore expected to be adaptable to many other nonlinear dissipative systems.
item.dc:creator: Vincent R. Martinez, Sarah Strikwerda, Xiang Wan

item.title: Lower Bounds for Stochastic First-Order Algorithms with Variance Reduction in Nonconvex--Concave Minimax Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.01662v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish complexity lower bounds for stochastic first-order algorithms in nonconvex--concave minimax optimization, allowing algorithms to use variance reduction. Our main contribution is a lower bound for a zero-respecting algorithm class that permits variance reduction, extending beyond the algorithmic restrictions imposed by some existing lower bounds. We consider objectives with an $L$-Lipschitz continuous joint gradient, a compact convex dual domain of Euclidean radius at most $D_Y$, and a primal value function, defined by maximizing the objective over the dual variable, with initial suboptimality at most $\Delta$. The target accuracy $\varepsilon$ is measured by the gradient norm of the Moreau envelope of the constrained primal value function with parameter $1/(2L)$. Under an unbiased stochastic first-order oracle with variance at most $\sigma^2$ and mean-squared smoothness, we prove the lower bound $\Omega\!\left(L^2D_Y\Delta\varepsilon^{-3}+L^3D_Y^2\Delta\sigma^2\varepsilon^{-6}\right)$. This result quantifies the dependence on accuracy, dual-domain radius, and oracle noise even when variance reduction is allowed. We also establish complementary lower bounds for nonconvex--strongly-concave minimax optimization. With dual strong-concavity parameter $\mu>0$ and condition number $\kappa:=L/\mu$, we obtain $\Omega\!\left(L\Delta\sqrt{\kappa}\,\varepsilon^{-2}+L\Delta\kappa\sigma^2\varepsilon^{-4}\right)$ under the bounded-variance oracle model. Under the additional mean-squared smoothness condition with constant $\bar L$, we obtain $\Omega\!\left(L\Delta\sqrt{\kappa}\,\varepsilon^{-2}+\Delta\bar L\sigma\kappa^{3/2}\varepsilon^{-3}\right)$. Together, these results identify complexity barriers across the concave and strongly concave regimes, with the main nonconvex--concave bound remaining valid for algorithms that use variance reduction.
item.dc:creator: Jiayi Song, Zi Xu

item.title: Fast Stochastic Post-Fault Replanning for Launch Vehicles under Persistent Parametric Uncertainty
item.description: arXiv:2610.02989v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Post-fault ascent replanning for launch vehicles requires rapid joint trajectory-guidance replanning under uncertainty to maintain closed-loop constraint satisfaction. In particular, propulsion performance cannot be promptly and fully identified after a fault, leaving persistent parametric uncertainty throughout the remaining flight. A fast stochastic ascent replanning method is developed to address this problem. To efficiently account for the cross-time correlation induced by persistent parametric uncertainty, a fast system level synthesis formulation is developed with a Riccati-based solution structure. The resulting feedback synthesis is complemented by a task-oriented terminal weighting method that shapes terminal covariance according to post-injection correction demand. These components are integrated with nominal trajectory replanning, chance-constraint tightening, and online feedback realization to establish a real-time joint stochastic trajectory-guidance replanning framework for launch vehicles. Nonlinear Monte Carlo simulations show that the proposed method effectively suppresses the influence of persistent parametric uncertainty and maintains stable convergence and high injection accuracy across parameter sweeps, with subsecond solution times. Compared with conventional ascent guidance, the empirical constraint-violation rate is substantially reduced.
item.dc:creator: Dai Shen, Chen Yang, Ziqi Xu, Lin Cheng, Hongbo Zhang, Hongtao Zheng, Shengping Gong

item.title: Global Extendability of Local Atoms in Sparse Moment Relaxations
item.description: arXiv:2610.17371v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Moment relaxations provide lower bounds for polynomial optimization problems, while their moment matrices can also carry information about solutions. We study whether atomic candidates extracted from clique blocks reveal part of a global minimizer in moment relaxations with correlative sparsity. We give sufficient conditions for global extendability. If the relaxation is value-exact and the moment matrix of a selected clique has maximum rank over the optimal face and satisfies simplicial regularity, then at least one of its atomic candidates is globally extendable. When this maximum rank is one, we derive a direct certificate for global extendability. Further examples demonstrate the necessity of value exactness for global extendability. Numerical experiments on unicycle trajectory optimization successfully yield near-optimal solutions through progressive extraction and fixing, demonstrating the practical effectiveness of the proposed approach.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Sun

item.title: Who pays for urban environment management? The role of the third-party service provider
item.description: arXiv:2610.32528v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The dominant contemporary paradigm of direct state-led urban environmental regulation entails significant risks, including high administrative burden, frequent conflicts with polluting entities, and economic vulnerabilities for those sources. To address these deficiencies, this paper integrates third-party service provider (TPSP) into China's existing management framework as a beneficial extension beyond conventional government intervention. Utilizing an evolutionary game approach, we compare two distinct institutional settings, a non-integration management mode and an integration management mode, and scrutinize the evolutionary dynamics across both two- and three-dimensional systems. To enhance system robustness, we embed a strategic behavior-based dynamic punishment mechanism that effectively eliminates the perturbing effects of varied penalty rules, thereby steering all stakeholders toward an ideal stable state. This comparative institutional analysis isolates the marginal contribution of third-party intermediation, specifies when outsourcing environmental services outperforms direct government enforcement, and reframes evolutionary game theory as a design device for institutional self-correction. Furthermore, a predefined variable importance analysis is conducted to highlight critical factors warranting attention in practical policy implementation. Extensive simulation experiments, carried out under diverse system-level and parameter-level conditions, validate the theoretical properties of our model. The findings offer concrete managerial insights to inform the formulation of more effective urban environmental supervision regulations.
item.dc:creator: Ke Han, Rui Wang, Samuel Ikemba

item.title: Quadratic Returns for a Moving Water Tank: An Explicit Right Inverse and a Sylvester Representation
item.description: arXiv:2610.35319v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Coron's return method established local nonlinear controllability of a moving water tank in sufficiently large time. The quadratic response at uniform equilibrium is studied in this work, where the acceleration input in the linearized model cannot excite the Fourier modes of the fluid with even indices. At three one-way wave crossings ($T=3$), the quadratic final-state map on a family of delayed controls that return the linearized state to zero is reduced to a scalar expression associated with a planar curve. A constant-level curve gives the return, and a tangential variation yields an explicit right inverse of the derivative of the quadratic final-state map. This inverse acts on all missing modes and maps mean-zero periodic $H^r$ targets to $H^r$ controls for every nonnegative integer $r$. A contraction argument also gives local exact solvability of the quadratic final-state equation. Finally, a time-dependent Sylvester equation provides an alternative representation of the coupling responsible for the second-order correction. The associated change of state coordinates involves one spatial derivative, while the control correction preserves regularity in appropriate Sobolev spaces. These results concern the first two variation equations only, while nonlinear controllability at this time remains open. Keywords: Controllability, control of partial differential equations, return method, Saint-Venant equations, Sylvester equations.
item.dc:creator: Constantinos Kitsos

item.title: Achieving Exponential Asymptotic Optimality in Average-Reward Restless Bandits without Global Attractor Assumption
item.description: arXiv:2405.17882v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the infinite-horizon average-reward restless bandit problem. We propose a novel two-set policy that maintains two dynamic subsets of arms: one subset of arms has a nearly optimal state distribution and takes actions according to an LP-Priority routine; the other subset of arms is driven towards the optimal state distribution and gradually merged into the first subset. We show that our two-set policy is asymptotically optimal with an $O(\exp(-C N))$ optimality gap for an $N$-armed problem, under the assumptions of aperiodic-unichain, non-degeneracy, and local stability. Our policy is the first to achieve exponential asymptotic optimality under the above set of easy-to-verify assumptions, whereas prior work either requires a global attractor assumption or only achieves an $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ optimality gap. We further discuss obstacles in weakening the assumptions by demonstrating examples where exponential asymptotic optimality is not achievable when any of the three assumptions is violated. Notably, we prove a lower bound for a large class of locally unstable restless bandits, showing that local stability is particularly fundamental for exponential asymptotic optimality. Finally, we use simulations to demonstrate that the two-set policy outperforms previous policies on certain restless bandit problems and performs competitively overall.
item.dc:creator: Yige Hong, Qiaomin Xie, Yudong Chen, Weina Wang

item.title: Sliced Wasserstein Geodesics and Equivalence Wasserstein and Sliced Wasserstein metrics
item.description: arXiv:2407.07219v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper will introduce a family of sliced Wasserstein geodesics which are not standard Wasserstein geodesics, objects yet to be discovered in the literature. These objects exhibit how the geometric structure of the Sliced Wasserstein space differs from the Wasserstein space, and provides a simple example of how solving the barycenter and gradient flow problems change when moving between these metrics. Some of these geodesics will only be H\"older continuous with respect to the Wasserstein metric and thus will provide a direct proof that Sliced-Wasserstein and regular Wasserstein metrics are not equivalent. Previous proofs of this were done for various cases in [2] and [5]. This paper, not only provides a direct proof, but also fills in gaps showing these metrics not equivalent in dimensions greater than 2.
item.dc:creator: John Seale Hopper

item.title: An Efficient Frequency-Based Approach for Maximal Square Detection in Binary Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2503.18974v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present FreqBased, a frequency-based algorithm for the maximal square problem in binary matrices. The algorithm maintains a vertical run-length array and a horizontal counter to validate candidate squares, matching the standard single-array dynamic programming algorithm in O(mn) time and O(n) space while reducing the amount of work performed during execution. Experiments on synthetic random binary matrices reveal a clear density-dependent performance transition: FreqBased consistently outperforms the dynamic programming baseline on moderate- and high-density inputs across Intel and AMD processors, achieving peak speedups of 1.175x and 1.277x, respectively, while executing up to 2.08x fewer instructions. On 180 real aerial image masks from the INRIA dataset, FreqBased outperforms the baseline on every instance with speedups of up to 4.63x, confirming that the instruction-count advantage observed on synthetic inputs extends to real binary matrices with spatial structure. Hardware performance counter analysis shows that the performance advantage arises primarily from reduced instruction count despite lower execution efficiency, demonstrating that algorithms with identical asymptotic complexity can exhibit substantially different practical performance depending on input characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Swastik Bhandari

item.title: Group Distributionally Robust Optimization with Flexible Sample Queries
item.description: arXiv:2505.15212v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Group distributionally robust optimization (GDRO) aims to learn models that perform well across $m$ distributions simultaneously. Existing methods either (i) query $m$ samples per round, which imposes strict implementation requirements, or (ii) query only a single sample per round, which requires many rounds to converge and therefore leads to long runtime. To avoid these limitations, we introduce a novel setting called \emph{flexible sample queries} (FSQ), which allows the number of samples that can be queried to vary across rounds. Under the FSQ setting, we cast GDRO as a two-player game: one performs non-oblivious online convex optimization, while the other tackles a non-oblivious prediction with limited advice (PLA) problem. In this game, the first player updates its decision using follow-the-regularized-leader with stochastic gradients. For the second player, we develop a new PLA method equipped with an adaptive exploration strategy that can leverage an arbitrary per-round sample size. We then establish the \emph{first} high-probability regret bound for non-oblivious PLA. By integrating these components, we develop an anytime GDRO algorithm that supports FSQ, and derive a high-probability optimization error bound of $O\left(\frac{1}{t}\sqrt{\sum_{j=1}^t \frac{m}{r_j}\log m}\right)$, where $r_j$ is the sample size at round $j$. This result demonstrates that the optimization error decreases as the per-round sample sizes increase, and implies the same near-optimal sample complexity of $O(m\log (m)/\epsilon^2)$ for any fixed sample size $r\in[m]$.
item.dc:creator: Haomin Bai, Dingzhi Yu, Shuai Li, Haipeng Luo, Lijun Zhang

item.title: Global Convergence of Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares for Robust Subspace Recovery
item.description: arXiv:2506.20533v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Robust subspace estimation is fundamental to many machine learning and data analysis tasks. Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares (IRLS) is an elegant and empirically effective approach to this problem, yet its theoretical properties remain poorly understood. This paper establishes that, under deterministic conditions, a variant of IRLS with dynamic smoothing regularization converges linearly to the underlying subspace from any initialization. We extend these guarantees to affine subspace estimation, a setting that lacks prior recovery theory. Additionally, we illustrate the practical benefits of IRLS through an application to low-dimensional neural network training. Our results provide the first global convergence guarantees for IRLS in robust subspace recovery and, more broadly, for nonconvex IRLS on a Riemannian manifold.
item.dc:creator: Gilad Lerman, Kang Li, Tyler Maunu, Teng Zhang

item.title: Stabilization and control of the semilinear hinged plate equation
item.description: arXiv:2511.17468v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article we prove semiglobal stabilization and exact controllability results for semilinear plate equations with hinged boundary conditions and analytic nonlinearity, when the damping or control acts on a region where the linear Schr\"odinger equation is observable. At the core of these results lies a new unique continuation property for the nonlinear plate equation, which significantly relaxes the geometric conditions required for such a property to hold. This property is obtained by combining recent results on propagation of analyticity in time and unique continuation for linear plate operators. More broadly, our approach exploits the linear observability of the plate equation to establish both stabilization and control results. First, we prove exponential decay of the nonlinear energy under a defocusing assumption on the nonlinearity. Second, under a weaker asymptotic assumption on the nonlinearity, we prove semiglobal exact control by analyzing control properties inside the compact attractor provided by the dynamics of the damped equation.
item.dc:creator: Crist\'obal Loyola

item.title: A modified Consensus-Based Optimization model: consensus formation and uniform-in-time propagation of chaos
item.description: arXiv:2511.19116v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a modified CBO model based on a regularized Gibbs weight. For each fixed temperature and regularization parameter, the regularized weight yields a configuration-independent lower bound on the denominator of the consensus map, thus a quantitative analysis without an upper bound on the objective function or cutoff in the noise. We first prove large-time consensus for the finite-particle system: above an explicit stability threshold, every particle converges exponentially to a common random limit. This consensus mechanism does not require the $C^2$ condition used in the direct weighted-energy argument. We next prove uniform-in-time propagation of chaos: we derive quantitative bounds for the finite-particle consensus point from finite-time concentration estimates for the mean-field law, with explicit approximation and large-time tail errors. The synchronous-coupling estimate also gives a quantitative comparison between the random particle consensus point and the deterministic mean-field consensus point. We also quantify the regularization error in the quantitative Laplace principle, making the effect of the additive regularization explicit. A direct weighted-energy estimate is obtained under stronger $C^2$ assumptions. Furthermore, we give a stopped quadratic stability estimate with the actual Gibbs denominator. Under the weak-landscape condition, full support of the initial law, and local nondegeneracy of the minimizer, we prove a high-probability finite-particle global-optimization theorem for any fixed $\lambda>\sigma^2$. The proof combines an affine-flow local-mass estimate, finite-time mean-field entrance, ordinary finite-horizon propagation of chaos, and an $\alpha$-independent convex trapping energy near the minimizer.
item.dc:creator: Young-Pil Choi, Seungchan Lee, Sihyun Song

item.title: Peng's Maximum Principle for Stochastic Delay Differential Equations of Mean-Field Type
item.description: arXiv:2512.00934v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend Peng's maximum principle to the case of stochastic delay differential equations of mean-field type. More precisely, the coefficients of our control problem depend on the state, on the past trajectory and on its expected value. Moreover, the control enters the noise coefficient and the control domain may be non-convex. Our approach is based on a lifting of the state equation to an infinite dimensional Hilbert space that removes the explicit delay in the state equation. The main ingredient in the proof of the maximum principle is a precise asymptotic for the expectation of the first order variational process, which allows us to neglect the corresponding second order terms in the expansion of the cost functional.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppina Guatteri, Federica Masiero, Lukas Wessels

item.title: Behavioral patterns and mean-field games in epidemiological models
item.description: arXiv:2512.20547v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a new type of Mean Field Game epidemiological models, in which subpopulations have different behavioral patterns: some people exhibit a type of ``rational'' self interested behavior by choosing Nash-equilibrium long-term strategies while others follow pre-specified ``non-rational'' patterns (e.g., either sticking to their usual habits or trying to mimic those around them). Our new B-MFG models allow for occasional behavioral switches, which rational individuals also take into account when formulating their Nash-equilibrium strategies. Although this modeling approach is general, here we develop it for individuals choosing their ``contact rates'' within a particular Susceptible-Infected-Recovered-Susceptible-Dead (SIRSD) epidemic model. The latter is based on a frequency-based force of infection with proportionate mixing and the mortality rate that rapidly increases once the proportion of infected individuals exceeds some prescribed threshold, resulting in a strain on medical resources. Numerical tests illustrate the properties of our model and highlight the ways in which additional/non-rational behavioral patterns and behavioral switching increase the impact of infectious diseases. The paper aims to build a bridge between two distinct communities of epidemiological modelers and to promote the consideration of behavioral patterns in broader Mean Field Games literature.
item.dc:creator: Finnegan Buckley, Alexander Vladimirsky

item.title: Inference-Time Alignment for Diffusion Models via Variationally Stable Doob's Matching
item.description: arXiv:2601.06514v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Inference-time alignment for diffusion models aims to adapt a pre-trained reference diffusion model toward a target distribution without retraining the reference score network, thereby preserving the generative capacity of the reference model while enforcing desired properties at inference time. A central mechanism for achieving such alignment is guidance, which modifies the sampling dynamics through an additional drift term. In this work, we introduce variationally stable Doob's matching, a novel framework for provable guidance estimation grounded in Doob's $h$-transform. Our approach formulates guidance as the gradient of the logarithm of an underlying Doob's $h$-function and employs gradient-regularized regression to simultaneously estimate both the $h$-function and its gradient, resulting in a consistent estimator of the guidance. Theoretically, we establish non-asymptotic convergence rates for the estimated guidance. Moreover, we analyze the resulting controllable diffusion processes and prove non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for the generated distributions in the Wasserstein-2 distance. Finally, we show that variationally stable guidance estimators are adaptive to unknown low dimensionality, effectively mitigating the curse of dimensionality under low-dimensional linear subspace assumptions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method and show the advantages compared to the baselines.
item.dc:creator: Jinyuan Chang, Chenguang Duan, Yuling Jiao, Ruoxuan Li, Yi Xu, Jerry Zhijian Yang

item.title: On the Reliability Limits of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Planning
item.description: arXiv:2603.26993v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: LLM-based multi-agent planning delegates operational decisions to specialists that communicate through finite reports. In this research, we study its reliability limits when a coordinator can revisit source records before completing a resource-constrained plan. A useful report can support an immediate decision or direct later reading, so its value depends on how these stages communicate. We derive exact communication and access tradeoffs and prove that two report forms suffice for a broad class of allocation requirements, one favoring immediate resource identification and the other distinguishing absence from unnamed availability. For shared capacity, this reduction permits joint optimization of reporting roles and adaptive reads for a fixed number of source types with unequal workloads and reading costs. Identical specialists can optimally report different facts, and maximizing immediate completion can impose an unbounded recovery cost penalty even with full-record access. We also conduct numerical experiments to quantify the benefits of the proposed joint optimization and show how source access improves language-agent decisions that already use their reports optimally. In particular, an exhaustive evaluation of 207,632 report designs on small allocation instances recovers the predicted joint optima. Our analysis suggests that reliable agent communication should be evaluated by the complete decisions it supports and the cost of finishing its unresolved cases, instead of solely by report length, local prediction accuracy, or immediate task completion, as is often the case in current practice.
item.dc:creator: Ruicheng Ao, Siyang Gao, David Simchi-Levi

item.title: Reinforcement Learning with Markov Risk Measures and Multipattern Risk Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2605.00654v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a risk-averse finite-horizon Markov Decision Process, we introduce a special class of Markov coherent risk measures, called mini-batch measures. We also define the class of multipattern risk-averse problems that reduce to linear MDPs in the risk-neutral case. We use both concepts in a feature-based $Q$-learning method with multipattern $Q$-factor approximation and we prove a high-probability regret bound of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\big(d^{3/2}HN^{H-1}\sqrt{K}\big)$, where $d$ is the number of features, $H$ is the horizon, $N\ge2$ is the mini-batch size, $K$ is the number of episodes, and $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}$ hides logarithmic factors.
